dz.headline: Algerian MPs limited to two questions monthly
dz.dek: The National People's Assembly has set a limit of two oral questions per deputy per month to streamline parliamentary oversight.
paragraphs: The National People's Assembly in Algeria has established a new rule limiting deputies to two oral questions per month directed at government ministers. This measure aims to regulate parliamentary oversight and manage the scheduling of ministerial responses, preventing the backlog of questions seen in previous legislative terms. Written questions, however, remain unlimited. The assembly's office is set to meet to review and schedule these oral questions for upcoming sessions.

This initiative is intended to organize the sessions dedicated to ministerial responses and ensure their timely programming, avoiding the accumulation of thousands of questions that occurred in past legislative periods. The new internal regulations also stipulate that the government must respond to both oral and written questions within a maximum of 30 days from the date of notification. If a minister claims lack of jurisdiction, the question will be redirected to the appropriate official.

Deputies are being advised to focus on the quality and relevance of their questions, ensuring they address citizens' concerns and national issues. The aim is to broaden parliamentary oversight to encompass various government sectors and policies, not solely local matters. Oral question sessions are typically held every two weeks, alternating between the National People's Assembly and the Council of the Nation, making the management of question numbers and scheduling crucial for effective oversight.

dz.headline: Algeria coach considers positional changes amid defensive shortages
dz.dek: Coach Ibrahim Hamdani is exploring shifting players to new roles to address a lack of central defenders before upcoming matches.
paragraphs: Algeria's national football team faces a critical shortage of central defenders following the retirement of Issa Mandi. Coach Ibrahim Hamdani is reportedly considering unconventional positional changes for players like Imad Abdelli or Touba to partner Ramy Bensebaini in defense. This move aims to find a stable and effective partnership, as previous pairings like Samir Chergui and Zouheir Belcide have shown limitations, contributing to goals conceded against weaker opponents.

In attack and midfield, Hamdani is under pressure to create a cohesive unit from available talent and establish consistent roles for players. Failure to do so could result in key players like Rayan Cherki and Ilan Kebbal being overlooked for selection due to established pairings. The coach has previously experimented successfully with players like Touba and Billel in wider defensive roles, indicating a willingness to adapt tactics.

The strategy of positional flexibility is not unique, with international coaches like Flick at Barcelona successfully converting wingers to strikers and even experimenting with midfielders in defense due to injury concerns. This approach views players as versatile assets capable of filling multiple roles without disrupting tactical plans, a philosophy Hamdani may adopt to overcome Algeria's current squad challenges.

dz.headline: Algerian social security agency adopts electronic signatures
dz.dek: The CNAS is preparing to integrate digital certification into its administrative processes to modernize operations and reduce paperwork.
paragraphs: Algeria's National Social Insurance Fund for Salaried Workers (CNAS) is moving towards digital document processing with the planned integration of electronic signatures. A meeting between the interim Director General of CNAS and the Director General of the Government Authority for Electronic Certification (AGCE) focused on implementing this digital certification into the document handling workflow.

This initiative is part of the CNAS's broader strategy to modernize its management systems and accelerate its digital transition. The move aims to streamline the processing of a large volume of documents handled by payment centers, progressively replacing paper with digital formats. This transition is expected to significantly lower administrative and technical burdens.

The collaboration between CNAS and AGCE marks a significant step in coordinating technical and organizational aspects for the project's launch. By adopting electronic signatures, the agency seeks to improve efficiency and reduce the operational costs associated with managing extensive paper-based records.

ao.headline: Japan explores Angola cooperation strategies
ao.dek: Japanese business delegation and Angolan minister discuss maritime transport, logistics, and financial services to boost national production.
paragraphs: Angola and Japan are exploring enhanced cooperation in key economic sectors, following a meeting in Luanda between Angolan Minister of Planning Victor Hugo Guilherme and a Japanese business delegation led by Ambassador Hiroaki Sano. The discussions focused on maritime transport, logistics, and financial services, areas identified as having significant potential to stimulate national production, improve goods distribution, and strengthen Angola's connections to regional markets.

Minister Guilherme highlighted food security and human capital development as national priorities, advocating for the adoption of new agricultural technologies, training of skilled personnel, and integrated development of economic corridors, including the Lobito and Southern Corridors. Sato Joji, executive director of the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) in Nairobi, expressed Japanese companies' interest in forming long-term partnerships focused on technology transfer, job creation, national capacity building, and value chain development.

The Japanese delegation also showed interest in visiting projects and infrastructure, with planned trips to Huambo province and areas along the Lobito Corridor to assess opportunities in productive sectors. Cooperation with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) on national cadre training was also discussed, signaling Angola's effort to attract investment that can expand domestic output and reduce reliance on oil revenues.

ao.headline: Angolan youth urged to manage finances
ao.dek: A new analysis aims to guide young Angolans toward financial literacy, encouraging savings, investment, and entrepreneurship.
paragraphs: Young Angolans are being encouraged to develop strong financial management skills, encompassing earning, saving, and investing, to secure their future. The analysis emphasizes that understanding individual finances is directly linked to responsible behavior and active citizenship. It questions whether the current focus is solely on income generation or also on the ability to manage, protect, and grow acquired resources.

Financial education aims to shift the perception of economic success away from visible consumption towards the value of financial stability, savings, investment, and wealth accumulation. This involves a cultural shift where young people learn to prioritize and control expenses, avoid excessive debt, and plan effectively for the long term.

The core principles of financial literacy involve earning through work and opportunity creation, managing through planning and expense control, and multiplying through savings, investment, and productive activities. This approach connects financial decisions to personal behavior, influencing how individuals interpret economic success and build a stable future.

ao.headline: Angolan NGOs demand local government legislation
ao.dek: Four civil society groups urged the National Assembly to prioritize and approve pending legislation for the immediate implementation of local government.
paragraphs: A coalition of Angolan non-governmental organizations, including OMUNGA, UPANGE, Friends of Angola, and ALDA, has expressed concern over delays in establishing local governments. In an open letter to the National Assembly, they cited President João Lourenço's statements on the upcoming municipal elections and stressed the constitutional imperative to institutionalize local authorities. The groups are calling for the immediate inclusion of remaining local government legislation on the current legislative agenda for discussion and approval.

The NGOs advocate for broad public consultation, involving civil society, traditional authorities, and citizens across Angola's 21 provinces. They believe this inclusive process is crucial for shaping the model of local governance. President Lourenço had previously urged opposition parties to resolve parliamentary impasses hindering the creation of elected local councils, stating that consensus among parliamentary groups is essential for moving forward.

The organizations argue that the lack of agreement on key aspects of the local government legislative package is the primary cause of the delay, potentially leading to a setback in the decentralization of power. They are pushing for consensus-building between the ruling MPLA party and the main opposition UNITA to finalize the process and implement the long-awaited local government structures.

ao.headline: Angola president promises end to hunger by 2027
ao.dek: President João Lourenço claims the ruling MPLA party will reveal a method for Angolans to live without eating by the next general election.
paragraphs: Angolan President João Lourenço has stated that the ruling MPLA party will present a definitive solution in 2027 to enable Angolans to live without food. This claim follows a case in India where a yogi, Prahlad Jani, reportedly survived for 14 days without ingesting or expelling anything, under observation by a team of doctors chosen by the Indian Ministry of Defense. The MPLA government suggests this method could be taught to Angolans to combat persistent hunger.

The evidence for Jani's abilities was previously explored in a 2006 Discovery Channel documentary, where scientists observed him for 10 days without concluding he was a fraud. Former President José Eduardo dos Santos had also previously theorized about Angolans living without eating, reportedly compelling citizens through hardship to pursue this path. Jani himself stated his health was perfect after the fast, attributing it to divine will.

Despite these claims, attempts by Angolans to follow Jani's method have reportedly resulted in death before achieving the desired outcome. The MPLA's promise for 2027 suggests a belief that the party can deliver a guaranteed truth, akin to how the Indian government investigated Jani's claims. The effectiveness of this proposed solution remains uncertain, with past voluntary attempts proving fatal.

ao.headline: Supreme Court unblocks politician's accounts
ao.dek: Mozambique's top court lifted a two-year freeze on Venâncio Mondlane's bank accounts, exposing flaws in the public prosecutor's case.
paragraphs: Mozambique's Supreme Court has ordered the unblocking of Venâncio Mondlane's bank accounts, which had been frozen for nearly two years. The court found that the freeze violated Mondlane's constitutional right to property, highlighting technical weaknesses in the Public Ministry's prosecution. This decision has raised questions about the integrity of the Mozambican justice system and its potential impact on regional and international perceptions.

The Public Ministry had frozen Mondlane's accounts based on allegations of conspiracy against state secrets and terrorism, using the Law on Extended Asset Loss and Asset Recovery. However, the Supreme Court's ruling indicated a failure by the prosecution to demonstrate a causal link between Mondlane's funds and the alleged criminal activities. This ruling serves as a significant setback for the prosecution and exposes investigative fragilities.

Mondlane intends to sue the Mozambican state from Lisbon for damages, a move that could create a sensitive diplomatic front and potentially affect foreign funding for the country. International law experts suggest this ruling could embolden regional human rights tribunals to question Mozambique's judicial credibility, particularly concerning the suppression of press freedom during Mondlane's trial.

bj.headline: Benin finance minister forecasts 300 billion CFA franc surplus
bj.dek: The minister of finance announced the projected surplus for public companies and offices in 2025 at a Cotonou accounting congress.
paragraphs: Benin's Minister of Finance announced a projected surplus of nearly 300 billion CFA francs for public companies and offices in 2025. The announcement was made at the 8th Congress of Accountants of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA), which began on October 21, 2026, in Cotonou. The congress, also marking the 20th anniversary of Benin's Order of Chartered Accountants, focuses on financial transparency and sovereignty within the UEMOA zone.

The event, held at the Cotonou Congress Center until October 22, 2026, gathered over 350 participants from more than 18 countries. Discussions centered on the theme 'The Accountant, Guarantor of Transparency and Financial Sovereignty in the UEMOA Space.' Experts, public officials, and economic actors shared knowledge on the role of accountants in state and business governance.

The Minister of Finance officially launched the proceedings, emphasizing the importance of reliable accounts in attracting investment, mobilizing savings, improving financing conditions, and strengthening decision-making capacity. The congress aims to generate operational recommendations to enhance financial governance and regional economic integration.

bj.headline: Benin lawmakers to review new road traffic code
bj.dek: Parliamentarians will consider proposed measures including legal alcohol limits and child restraint systems during the current session.
paragraphs: Benin's National Assembly will examine a draft road traffic code during its second ordinary session, which began on October 21, 2026. The announcement was made by the assembly's president, Joseph Djogbénou, at the session's opening. Lawmakers participated in a preparatory seminar in Grand-Popo on October 20, engaging with government officials and road safety experts to ready the text for review.

Key proposals within the draft code include establishing a legal blood alcohol content limit, cracking down on driving under the influence of drugs, and addressing excessive speeding. The code also aims to introduce child restraint systems, enhance road safety education in schools, and impose stricter penalties for hit-and-run offenses and failure to obey orders.

The preparatory discussions also covered control mechanisms and sanction scales. The draft legislation will undergo committee review before a plenary session debate. These measures are currently part of a proposed bill and have not yet been enacted.

bj.headline: Cotonou closes city hall access for road work
bj.dek: Road construction on streets 12 007 and 12 048 will block access to Cotonou's city hall for three months starting October 26.
paragraphs: Access routes to Cotonou's city hall will be closed for three months beginning Monday, October 26, 2026, due to ongoing road construction. The closures affect access points from Boulevard de la Marina and Avenue Jean-Paul II. The announcement comes from the Société des infrastructures routières et de l’aménagement du territoire (SIRAT) in a statement dated October 20.

The road closures are a direct result of the commencement of work on streets 12 007 and 12 048, which are located around the city hall currently under construction. These infrastructure improvements are part of the Asphaltage 1 B project. SIRAT has stated that measures will be put in place to ensure residents can still reach their homes and places of business.

SIRAT has outlined specific arrangements to maintain access for residents and businesses during the construction period. The public is urged to adhere to safety regulations, observe speed limits, and follow the directions provided by traffic agents and the Republican Police.

bj.headline: Ligue Pro du Bénin names media commission
bj.dek: The Benin Professional Football League has appointed a new ad hoc media commission to improve relations with clubs and journalists.
paragraphs: The Benin Professional Football League (LFPB) has established a new ad hoc media commission, with its members appointed by LFPB President Joël Debally on October 20, 2026, in Cotonou. The commission's primary objective is to enhance the relationship between the LFPB, its clubs, and media professionals. It will also focus on improving the conditions under which media cover league competitions, including streamlining accreditation processes, stadium access, and match-day coordination.

To ensure information reaches all parts of the country, the commission will work with six regional correspondents. The appointed members include Eddy Rabin as president, Hamadou Issa as LFPB communication representative, Salomon Singbo for Ligue 1 clubs, Bienvenu Azoma for Ligue 2 clubs, Pascal Hounkpatin representing the media, Maurice Zounon overseeing accreditations and press relations, and Claude Diogninou responsible for match security.

The regional correspondents appointed are Nouhoum A. Biaou for Atacora-Donga, Bruno Agassounon for Atlantique-Littoral, Aliou Toundé for Borgou-Alibori, Adrien Amoussou for Mono-Couffo, Edmond Houssikinde for Ouémé-Plateau, and Élisée Hounkpatin for Zou-Collines. This structure aims to create a more organized and accessible media environment for the league's events.

bw.headline: Botswana secures South African beef market access
bw.dek: The agreement allows for exports of processed beef and live cattle, providing farmers with a new market amid disease and drought concerns.
paragraphs: Botswana has successfully negotiated access to the South African market for its beef and live cattle exports. This development offers a crucial new avenue for the country's livestock farmers, who are currently facing pressure from foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) and the threat of drought.

Director of Veterinary Services Dr. Kobedi Segale confirmed that discussions with South African authorities commenced in August. The resulting agreement encompasses both processed beef and live cattle, provided they meet the necessary veterinary and export requirements stipulated by South Africa.

This market access comes at a critical time for Botswana's agricultural sector. The dual threats of FMD and potential drought have created an urgent need for alternative markets to support livestock producers and ensure the stability of the sector.

bw.headline: Botswana ranks third in Africa on global capitalism index
bw.dek: The nation scored 72.7 out of 100, but faces persistent barriers to private-sector growth.
paragraphs:
Botswana has been ranked as Africa

's third-highest-performing capitalist economy, according to the Global Capitalism Index. The country achieved a score of 72.7 out of 100 in the index released by the University of Virginia

's Democracy and Capitalism Lab. This places Botswana behind Mauritius and Seychelles, which ranked first and second respectively in Africa.

Globally, Botswana secured the 52nd position. Namibia followed in fourth place among African nations with a score of 69.7. Despite its strong overall performance, the index highlighted existing weaknesses in business formation and capital markets.

These identified weaknesses suggest that persistent barriers continue to hinder the growth of Botswana's private sector. The index aims to measure various aspects of capitalist economies, with scores reflecting their overall performance and health.

bw.headline: Nurses union condemns clinic's 24-hour service rollout
bw.dek: The Botswana Nurses Union says Sefhophe Clinic's expansion to round-the-clock care is unsafe due to insufficient staff.
paragraphs: The Botswana Nurses Union (BONU) has voiced strong objections to the recent transition of Sefhophe Clinic to a 24-hour facility, citing significant concerns over patient safety and staff working conditions. BONU argues that the service expansion was implemented prematurely, without the necessary personnel to manage continuous operations and emergency responses effectively.

According to the union, the clinic is currently staffed by only five nurses and a single midwife. This limited team is deemed inadequate to meet the demands of round-the-clock healthcare, including attending to emergencies and fulfilling the medical needs of the surrounding communities. BONU believes this staffing level compromises the quality of care provided.

The union's statement highlights a critical gap between the operational requirements of a 24-hour health service and the available resources at Sefhophe Clinic. BONU's condemnation suggests a potential risk to both patients and the existing healthcare staff due to the strain of inadequate staffing.

bw.headline: Botswana Housing Corporation reverses P101.7mn loss
bw.dek: The corporation anticipates a P49.58 million profit before tax for the 2025/2026 financial year, marking a significant turnaround.
paragraphs: Botswana Housing Corporation (BHC) expects to return to profitability in the 2025/2026 financial year, projecting a P49.58 million profit before tax. This follows a substantial P101.741 million loss recorded in the previous financial year. The anticipated improvement represents a P151.321 million turnaround, according to a cautionary statement issued by the corporation on October 13.

The turnaround is attributed to internal adjustments and improved financial management within the corporation. BHC has been undergoing restructuring aimed at enhancing operational efficiency and service delivery. The corporation's statement indicates a positive outlook for its financial performance in the coming fiscal period.

This financial recovery is crucial for BHC's ongoing projects and its ability to meet housing demands across the country. The projected profit will enable further investment in infrastructure development and housing initiatives, supporting the government's broader economic and social development agenda.

bw.headline: Botswana inflation eases to 7.8 percent
bw.dek: Botswana's annual inflation rate fell by 1.5 percentage points in September, offering some relief from rising costs.
paragraphs: Botswana's annual inflation rate declined sharply to 7.8 percent in September from 9.3 percent in August. The decrease of 1.5 percentage points offers some relief to consumers and businesses facing elevated operating costs. Statistics Botswana's Consumer Price Index report for September 2026 detailed the fall, noting that transport costs remained the primary driver of price increases across the economy.

The easing inflation rate provides a welcome respite for households and companies that have been struggling with the financial impact of rising prices. While the overall inflation has decreased, the persistent increases in transport costs continue to affect economic activity and household budgets.

The September figures indicate a positive trend in price stability, although the underlying causes of transport cost increases require ongoing attention. This development is a key indicator for economic health and consumer confidence in Botswana.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso and Turkey discuss defense pact
bf.dek: Officials from both nations met in Ankara to explore enhanced cooperation in security, health, and economic sectors.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso and Turkey are negotiating a defense and security agreement following the first session of political consultations held in Ankara on October 20, 2026. The discussions, led by Burkina Faso's Ambassador Hermann Yirigouin Toé and Turkey's Ambassador Volkan Isikci, covered a broad spectrum of bilateral cooperation, including education, health, agriculture, industrial development, mining, and energy.

In the health sector, Burkina Faso's delegation praised Turkey's support for national renal transplant training and requested a fast-track visa system for patients needing emergency medical evacuation. The aim is to reduce medical expatriation and strengthen domestic healthcare infrastructure. On regional security, Ambassador Toé highlighted the geopolitical shifts in the Sahel, including the formation of the Sahel States Confederation (AES), and urged Turkey to partner in combating terrorism.

Ambassador Isikci reaffirmed Turkey's commitment to supporting Burkina Faso's security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity. The Turkish delegation expressed a desire for a formal defense and security accord and proposed a partnership convention between the diplomatic institutes of both countries. Both sides also acknowledged the potential for increased economic and trade exchanges.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso police adapt to evolving threats
bf.dek: Ouagadougou hosts annual police commissioners' conference to address rising crime and digital offenses.
paragraphs: The sixth annual conference of police commissioners opened in Ouagadougou on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, under the theme "The Popular Progressive Revolution, a lever for reforming the National Police: adaptability, challenges and prospects." The meeting aims to assess the institution's achievements and formulate recommendations to enhance service efficiency.

National Police Director General Thierry Dofizouho Tuina stated that the conference is particularly important given the evolving threats, diversifying criminal phenomena, and the need to continuously adapt institutional responses to territorial realities. He emphasized that the meeting will critically examine the National Police's successes, shortcomings, and challenges, aligning with the ideals of the popular progressive revolution.

Minister of State for Territorial Administration, Émile Zerbo, representing the Prime Minister, highlighted that security is essential for institutional stability, population protection, and economic development. He stressed that the National Police's transformation must focus on adaptability to changing threats, performance in meeting public needs, and exemplary leadership.

bf.headline: Poura CEB teacher receives motorcycle for perfect exam results
bf.dek: Bouma Nebié was awarded a motorcycle and cash for achieving a 100% pass rate for his 59 students in the 2026 CEP exams.
paragraphs: The top-performing teacher in Poura's basic education district (CEB), Bouma Nebié, received a motorcycle and a financial envelope on October 17, 2026. Nebié, from Poura-Mine D school, achieved a 100% success rate for his 59 students in the 2026 Certificat d’études primaires (CEP) exams. The award ceremony, held during the CEB's excellence day, also recognized top students and other outstanding teachers.

Fatim Ouedraogo, from Poura-Mine « B » school, was named the best student in the CEB with an average of 9.06. Top students in CP1 through CM1 classes each received a school kit, while the top three CM2 students were awarded a bicycle and a school kit. Three internally displaced students were also encouraged with school kits, and intermediate class teachers received envelopes and congratulatory letters.

The best school award went to Poura-Mine D, which also achieved a 100% CEP pass rate under the leadership of Sibiri Zoma. The event was sponsored by local mining operator Kibsa Sawadogo and attended by Poura's special delegation president, Momini Sawadogo, who pledged continued support for educational goals. The ceremony featured student performances and a show by artist Desko 1er.

bi.headline: Paris loses to Barcelona in four-goal thriller
bi.dek: Two early injuries to key players did not deter Paris from a spirited comeback, ultimately falling short in a high-scoring match.
paragraphs: The match began with an immediate threat from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, whose shot struck the post within the first two minutes. However, the game took a turn when Paris lost two players to injury: Ousmane Dembélé in the 19th minute and Dani Olmo in the 27th minute. Despite these setbacks, young talent Désiré Doué opened the scoring for Paris in the 38th minute with a precise strike.

In the second half, Barcelona, previously undefeated under coach Hansi Flick, equalized in the 55th minute through Xavi Espart's powerful shot. Paris faced further challenges as Marquinhos and Kvaratskhelia were forced off, leaving their team vulnerable. Yet, Lucas Hernandez headed in a goal from a corner in the 72nd minute to put Paris back in the lead.

The lead was short-lived as Barcelona's Lamine Yamal scored in the 79th minute, bringing the score to 2-2. The match concluded with Barcelona securing a 4-2 victory, despite Paris's resilience and earlier efforts to overcome injuries and the deficit.

bi.headline: Burundi death certificate questions agency premises
bi.dek: An administrative document states a Burundi Development Agency official died at home, but his actual place of death was the agency's office.
paragraphs: An administrative certificate stating that Bruce Sebanza, an official at the Burundi Development Agency (ADB), died at home has raised questions. The document, confirmed as authentic by sources, designates the ADB's director general, Dr. Révérien Nizigiyimana, as the death declarant. However, the certificate states Sebanza died "at home (within the premises of the A.D.B.)" on October 13, 2026, despite his actual residence being in a different part of Bujumbura.

The discrepancy between Sebanza's registered address in Mutakura and the ADB's location in Mutanga Nord, both in the northern part of the capital, casts doubt on the circumstances under which the certificate was issued. Nizigiyimana's role as declarant is also notable, as his name has been previously linked to testimonies concerning events preceding Sebanza's death, prompting calls for a rigorous examination of his involvement.

This administrative attestation follows a call by the Independent National Human Rights Commission for investigations into the matter. The certificate does not replace a judicial inquiry to establish the exact causes of death and any potential responsibilities. Judicial authorities are expected to conduct thorough, independent, and impartial investigations.

bi.headline: Saido Berahino retires from English football to coach Burundi
bi.dek: The former West Bromwich Albion striker returns to his birth nation to train the national team, the Intamba Mu Rugamba.
paragraphs: Saido Berahino has announced his retirement from professional football in England, concluding a career that began in the streets of Bujumbura. He expressed deep gratitude to West Bromwich Albion, stating that football has given him everything, from his early days as a refugee to playing in the Premier League. Berahino reflected on the highs and lows of his career, acknowledging the harsh lessons learned at the highest level of the sport.

The decision to hang up his boots comes not from weariness but from a sense of accomplishment, as Berahino prepares for a new chapter. He declared that football has remained his constant pillar throughout his life. His return to Burundi signifies a desire to give back to the nation where his journey began.

Berahino will now serve the Burundian national team, the Intamba Mu Rugamba, not as a distant figurehead but as an active coach on the field. This move marks a full circle for the player, transitioning from a refugee child to a coach for his home country's team.

bi.headline: Burundi refugees ordered back to camps
bi.dek: Authorities cite security concerns for the order, but refugees fear loss of income and increased hardship.
paragraphs: Burundi's Office for Refugees and Stateless Persons (ONPRA) is compelling refugees living outside designated camps to return to their original settlements. ONPRA coordinator Richard Uwimana stated the measure is intended to enhance security and control over the refugee population amidst regional instability. This directive follows the recent public presentation of 13 individuals, primarily Banyamulenge refugees, accused of espionage for Rwanda and armed groups in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The decision has sparked anger and worry among refugees who rely on activities outside the camps for their livelihoods. With reduced humanitarian aid and insufficient food rations, many families depend on small businesses, day labor, or other income-generating ventures in urban areas like Bujumbura to supplement their essential needs. A refugee selling clothes in Bujumbura expressed concern that the order will eliminate his primary source of income.

The government's push for refugees to return to camps is framed as a security imperative, particularly after accusations of spying were leveled against Banyamulenge refugees. However, the refugees themselves argue that these measures threaten their survival by cutting off vital income streams. Some relatives of those accused have dismissed the charges as unjust, stating the individuals fled conflict in South Kivu to protect their lives.

cm.headline: Cameroon seeks UK finance for timber processing
cm.dek: Yaoundé wants British support to modernize its timber industry, focusing on small businesses and technology upgrades.
paragraphs: Cameroon is pursuing financial and technological assistance from the United Kingdom to upgrade its timber-processing sector, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The Ministry of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, Social Economy and Handicrafts (MINPMEESA) discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation in local timber processing, developing forestry SMEs, modernizing equipment, and transferring technology with UK forestry adviser Neil Scotland. The initiative aims to boost domestic processing and reduce reliance on raw wood exports.

Discussions also covered mobilizing financing tailored to Cameroonian businesses, though no specific financial commitments or timelines were announced. Scotland, Senior Forestry Adviser at the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), was joined by Deputy British High Commissioner Samantha Smith and Regional Climate and Environment Adviser Euan McCarthy. The meeting highlighted Cameroon's goal to make responsible forest resource management a driver of growth and sustainable development.

This effort is exemplified by the SMEs Wood's Park project in Lomié, which aims to foster SMEs, artisans, and social economy organizations, creating jobs and higher-value products. cm.headline: Cameroon delays IMF talks, risking budget support
cm.dek: The nation has not formally requested negotiations for a new economic program, jeopardizing CFA300 billion in potential 2027 budget aid.
paragraphs: Cameroon has yet to initiate formal discussions with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a new economic program, a delay that puts CFA300 billion in planned 2027 budget support at risk. Finance Minister Louis-Paul Motaze stated that he has presented the case for renewed negotiations to Cameroonian authorities and is awaiting their response before commencing discussions, though no timeline has been provided. This delay has persisted for several months since Motaze first called for a new IMF program at a cabinet meeting in October 2025, following the expiration of a previous agreement.

The proposal for a new IMF program was expected to be submitted to President Paul Biya for a decision. Despite the finance minister's continued support for a new agreement nearly a year later, the government has not yet taken the necessary formal steps to begin negotiations. This inaction contrasts with other Central African countries that have made commitments to renew their cooperation with the IMF.

The potential budget support is crucial for the nation's financial planning. The lack of formal engagement with the IMF signifies a significant hurdle in securing this vital funding, which is contingent upon reaching an agreement with the international financial institution. The government's next steps are critical in determining whether this financial support will materialize.

cm.headline: MP3 congratulates Noah on MRC presidency
cm.dek: The Mouvement patriotique pour la prospérité du peuple (MP3) has sent its best wishes to Tiriane Balbine Noah following her election as the new leader of the Mouvement pour la.
paragraphs: The Mouvement patriotique pour la prospérité du peuple (MP3) on October 20 sent enthusiastic congratulations to Tiriane Balbine Noah, who was elected president of the Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun (MRC) on October 17. Noah replaces Maurice Kamto and her election has prompted reactions from opposition parties. The MP3, led by Hiram Samuel Iyodi, praised Noah and the new national bureau, calling the MRC's convention a lesson in democracy for other political parties.

The MP3 expressed hope that this new chapter for the MRC will strengthen democratic pluralism, debate, and citizen participation in Cameroon. The party also highlighted a shared responsibility with the MRC to work towards a more just, free, and prosperous Cameroon where public action prioritizes the general interest. This shared goal is exemplified by both parties' refusal to recognize the official results of the October 12, 2025, presidential election, asserting the need to respect the people's will.

This shared stance and potential for collaboration could lead the two distinct parties to form strategic alliances. The upcoming legislative and municipal elections present the first opportunity for the MP3 and MRC to work together. The MP3 wishes the new MRC leadership success in continuing their predecessors' work and navigating challenges that may affect the party's influence.

cm.headline: World Bank launches digital strategy for Africa
cm.dek: The institution aims to boost connectivity, affordable devices, skills, and AI readiness to create jobs for a growing youth population.
paragraphs: The World Bank Group unveiled its first digital strategy for Africa and developing nations on October 20, 2026, in Seoul. The plan focuses on four key areas: connectivity, affordable devices, digital skills, and artificial intelligence. This initiative is critical for Africa, where only 23 percent of people in low-income countries use the internet, highlighting a significant digital divide.

The strategy aims to help developing countries expand affordable access to digital services and create jobs. World Bank President Ajay Banga stated that digital technologies can help countries generate employment and optimize limited resources. This comes as one point two billion young people in developing nations are expected to enter the workforce in the next 10 to 15 years, with only 420 million jobs projected.

The plan includes developing reliable connectivity from undersea cables to homes, schools, and health centers. It also supports making devices and data more affordable through partnerships, developing digital services and skills for employment, and strengthening readiness for AI, particularly "small AI" tools suited for local conditions. The strategy also emphasizes data protection, cybersecurity, and fraud prevention.

cm.headline: Cameroon plans CFA8.8 billion organic fertilizer plant
cm.dek: TMG International Investment Group and PT Turrima Agro Mass are considering a project to produce fertilizer locally and reduce import reliance.
paragraphs: Cameroonian firm TMG International Investment Group PLC and Indonesia’s PT Turrima Agro Mass are exploring a $15 million (CFA8.8 billion) organic fertilizer plant in Cameroon. The project aims to replace some fertilizer imports with local production. Indonesia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced the potential investment on October 19, 2026, following a memorandum of understanding signed on October 16 between the two companies regarding agricultural technology transfer and local production capacity development.

The proposed factory will be part of a 25-hectare integrated agricultural complex. This complex is planned to include laboratories, raw material storage and processing facilities, and areas for crop cultivation and livestock farming. The partners intend to utilize organic waste from agricultural and livestock activities as the primary input for fertilizer production.

The Indonesian ministry stated the $15 million figure represents the potential value of the fertilizer plant project. However, the ministry did not provide a breakdown of how this amount would be allocated between industrial equipment and other facilities within the larger agricultural complex.

cf.headline: Central African Republic hosts 23rd medical exams
cf.dek: More than 600 participants from various African countries are in Bangui for the 23rd session of the Council of African and Malagasy Higher Education (CAMES) aggregation exams.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic is hosting the 23rd session of the aggregation exams in human and animal medicine, organized by the Council of African and Malagasy Higher Education (CAMES). The official launch ceremony took place in Bangui on October 19, 2026, with the exams running from October to November. Over 600 participants are attending, including nine candidates from the Central African Republic, an increase from previous years. Those who pass will attain the rank of university professor.

A delegation from the CAMES General Secretariat visited the Central African Republic from October 18 to 21, 2026, to assess teaching methods and quality at the University of Bangui. The delegation met with the rector of the university and the minister of Higher Education. Boniface Koffi, president of the jury coordination, noted the progress in the country's participation, highlighting the increased number of female candidates.

The exams aim to promote qualified teacher-researchers capable of training new generations, advancing research, and meeting human resource needs in health sectors. The process includes online preliminary tests and in-person evaluations in Bangui from November 10 to 18. The CAMES emphasizes ethical conduct and impartiality from the juries, with the goal of improving human and animal health sectors.

cf.headline: Civil society leaders on hunger strike in gendarmerie
cf.dek: Five Central African Republic civil society leaders are on a hunger strike in gendarmerie custody after being denied food and water by police.
paragraphs: Five Central African Republic civil society leaders arrested on October 15 in Bangui have begun a hunger strike at the gendarmerie. Their health is a concern for investigators, who are now angry with police colleagues. The leaders were detained by police for two days without food or water before being transferred to the gendarmerie in a weakened state.

The transfer of the five detained civil society leaders to the gendarmerie's Section de recherche et d’investigation (SRI) has angered several gendarmes. The detainees, including Quentin Claver Ngouando of the iGwé movement and Élysée Nguemale of the OGDC, are now refusing food and water in protest of their treatment.

The five individuals are Quentin Claver Ngouando, Élysée Nguemale, Stève Bendo Deny, Barry Mardios, and Igor Mokpem. Their detention and subsequent hunger strike highlight tensions between different branches of law enforcement and raise concerns about the treatment of civil society figures in the country.

cf.headline: Cameroon truckers resume Central African Republic fuel deliveries
cf.dek: Road traffic between Cameroon and the Central African Republic has restarted after a two-week strike by truckers protesting harassment by security forces.
paragraphs: Cameroonian transporters resumed their activities on October 20, ending a two-week strike that had halted the flow of fuel to the Central African Republic. The strike, which began in early October, was a protest against road harassment attributed to Central African security forces. During the stoppage, over 300 fuel tankers were immobilized at the border, impacting supply chains in both nations.

The resumption of traffic follows mediation talks held in Yaoundé between Cameroonian and Central African authorities. Both governments agreed to address the transporters' grievances to facilitate the return to normal operations. The first fuel tankers have since crossed the border at Cantonnier, heading towards Bangui, signaling a gradual restoration of fuel supplies.

Local officials, including the governor of Cameroon's East region and the sub-prefect of Baboua, met with transporters at Garoua-Boulaï to ensure a smooth restart. Assurances were given regarding the security of Cameroonian drivers in Central African territory, a key demand of the truckers. The transporters have committed to resuming their usual routes, aiming to re-establish the country's fuel supply.

cf.headline: Newtech Institut graduates celebrate academic success
cf.dek: The Bangui-based institute awarded diplomas from bachelor's to master's degrees, recognizing top students and a robotics champion.
paragraphs: Newtech Institut in Bangui celebrated its 2026 academic year with an open house, solemn opening ceremony, and graduation for the Émilie Béatrice Epaye class on Saturday, October 17. Diplomas were conferred for studies ranging from Baccalaureate to Master's levels. The event also honored Charline Girardot, a student recognized for her achievements in a South Korean robotics competition.

Serge Singha Bengba, President Founder of Newtech, congratulated students on their excellent national exam results, emphasizing education as a crucial investment for the country's future. He also acknowledged the dedication of teachers and parents. Charline Girardot, the institute's top student, was highlighted for her academic excellence, including a Baccalaureate in the challenging Series C, and her representation of the Central African Republic in the international robotics contest.

The institute's strategic decision to integrate robotics and artificial intelligence into its scientific curriculum from the secondary level was reiterated. The promotion was named in honor of Émilie Béatrice Epaye, recognizing her distinguished career as a four-time elected deputy, minister, and her past achievements as a track and field athlete and academic.

cf.headline: Central African Republic hosts second African boxing tournament
cf.dek: Bangui prepares to welcome athletes from Cameroon, Gabon, and Congo for a multi-category boxing event.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic's capital, Bangui, is set to host the second edition of the African Boxing Tournament. The event, organized by Bamara Boxe Pro Academy, Almadina Groupe, and Maison Russe, will feature professional, semi-professional, and amateur bouts. Athletes from Cameroon, Gabon, and Congo will compete alongside local boxers, aiming to elevate the sport's profile in the nation.

A key highlight will be the 75kg professional fight between Central African Republic's Kevin Dasso and Cameroon's Kola Sucré. The program also includes two semi-professional and four amateur fights, showcasing emerging talents like Hergy Betoumbam and Merveil Amoloma. The tournament aims to provide Central African boxers with an international platform and prepare them for future competitions, including the Olympics.

The tournament is scheduled for October 31 at the Omnisports Stadium in Bangui. Kevin Dasso expressed confidence and called for support from sponsors and fans. Maison Russe, a partner, stated its commitment to athlete development and increasing the sport's visibility. The event seeks to establish the Central African Republic as a hub for sporting talent on the continent.

km.headline: SONELEC improves electricity supply and finances
km.dek: The national electricity company has reduced monthly losses and increased daily supply hours across the islands.
paragraphs: The Comorian national electricity company, SONELEC, has reported significant financial recovery and improved electricity provision following widespread outages in 2024. Presenting its performance from February 2025 to October 2026, the company highlighted a reduction in monthly losses on Ngazidja from 250 million Comorian francs to 22 million by 2025, with a positive monthly result of 100 million francs in the second quarter of 2026. Sales rose by 7% to 15.2 billion francs in 2025.

Electricity supply has seen uneven improvements across the islands. Ngazidja now receives an average of 20 hours of electricity daily, up from 18 hours and 42 minutes in 2025. Anjouan's supply reached 18 hours and 19 minutes in September, while Mohéli maintains continuous power. Solar energy now accounts for nearly 20% of production in 2026, up from 9.6% in 2024, saving the company approximately 135 million francs in diesel costs between January and September.

Despite these gains, thermal power generation remains constrained, with only 23 megawatts available out of 41.6 installed. SONELEC plans to invest 33 billion francs between 2027 and 2029 to modernize equipment and upgrade the network, supported by a $57 million World Bank loan. The company aims to provide at least 23 hours of electricity daily nationwide without evening load shedding by 2027.

cg.headline: Congo minister reaffirms commitment to human rights
cg.dek: Aimé Ange Wilfrid Bininga attended a continental meeting in Dakar, stressing ongoing efforts are needed to protect fundamental rights.
paragraphs: The Republic of Congo's Justice Minister, Aimé Ange Wilfrid Bininga, participated in the 89th ordinary session of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights in Dakar, Senegal. Leading an official delegation, Bininga engaged in discussions focused on promoting and protecting human rights across Africa. He acknowledged the progress made by Congo in this area but emphasized that continuous effort and commitment from public authorities and all stakeholders are essential for the effective protection of human rights.

The minister's presence at the session served as an opportunity for Congo to contribute to dialogues concerning the challenges in upholding fundamental rights, strengthening protection mechanisms, and fulfilling commitments made by African states. The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, an organ of the African Union, works to promote and protect human rights on the continent.

The commission's ordinary sessions provide a platform for state representatives, national human rights institutions, and civil society organizations to review advancements and persistent difficulties. Bininga's participation underscores Congo's engagement with continental efforts to address human rights issues and reinforce protective measures.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast completes 220 child labor actions
ci.dek: A joint initiative by Solidaridad West Africa and Olam Food Ingredients has reported an 88% execution rate on planned actions against child labor.
paragraphs: Solidaridad West Africa and Olam Food Ingredients have completed 220 of 251 planned actions against child labor in Ivory Coast's cocoa sector. This represents an 88% execution rate for the initiative, which concluded its activities with a workshop in Cocody on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. The program, known as the Child Labor Monitoring and Remediation System (CLMRS), was deployed in July 2025 and covered 10 cooperatives within Olam Food Ingredients' supply chain.

The CLMRS initiative aimed to monitor and address instances of child labor within the cocoa farming communities. The system's implementation involved working directly with cooperatives to identify and remediate issues related to child labor, ensuring compliance with ethical sourcing standards. The workshop served as a platform to present the final results and discuss the impact of the program.

Olam Food Ingredients, a global leader in food and beverage ingredients, partnered with Solidaridad West Africa to implement this system. The focus on the cocoa supply chain highlights the sector's vulnerability to child labor and the efforts being made by major industry players to combat it. The program's success is measured by the number of actions taken and the coverage of cooperatives within the supply chain.

ci.headline: Camara elected Ivory Coast Senate president
ci.dek: Kandia Kamissoko Camara, a former English teacher and minister, has been elected president of the Ivorian Senate.
paragraphs: Kandia Kamissoko Camara, born in Abidjan in 1959, assumed the presidency of the Senate of Ivory Coast on October 12, 2023. She is also the mayor of Abobo. Before her current role, Camara had a career as an English teacher for nearly 20 years and served as the minister of National Education for a decade. She was also the first woman to lead the country's foreign affairs.

Camara's background includes a notable period as a competitive handball player, winning the Ivorian championship in 1974 and 1980, and the African Clubs Champions Cup in 1981. After her athletic career, she pursued higher education, earning an English degree from the University of Abidjan and a certificate in advanced education studies from the University of Lancaster in England. She began teaching in 1983.

Her political journey began with the Ivorian Popular Front (PDCI) before she joined the Rally of Republicans (RDR) in 1994. Camara held significant positions within the RDR's women's wing and served as a special advisor to the Prime Minister. In 2011, she was appointed Minister of National Education, a position she held until April 2021, overseeing technical education and vocational training during her tenure.

ci.headline: 12 charged over gendarme killing amid election tensions
ci.dek: Authorities have charged 12 people with murder and terrorism in connection with the death of a gendarme last year.
paragraphs: 12 people have been charged and remanded in custody over the killing of a gendarme, an incident that occurred one year after deadly election-related violence in Ivory Coast. Prosecutor Oumar Braman Koné announced the charges on Tuesday, stating the suspects admitted involvement in the shooting of Second Lieutenant Daniogo Klênon Lacina on October 20, 2025, while he patrolled near Agboville. The alleged shooter confessed to opening fire on security forces.

The accused face serious charges including murder, terrorist acts, conspiracy against state authority, and participation in an insurrectionary movement. The case has been transferred to Abidjan’s anti-terrorism division. This investigation unfolds against a backdrop of lingering political tensions following President Alassane Ouattara’s disputed fourth-term election victory last year, an event that officially claimed 11 lives.

The opposition party PPA-CI has accused the government of anti-democratic actions, though authorities maintain the prosecutions are not politically motivated. The gendarme’s death and subsequent charges highlight the ongoing security concerns and political instability in the country.

eg.headline: Egypt reclaims over 3.5 million feddans of desert for agriculture
eg.dek: The state has added millions of feddans of agricultural land through desert reclamation, aiming for self-sufficiency and affordable food.
paragraphs: Egypt's Agriculture Minister Alaa Farouk stated that the nation has reclaimed over 3.5 million feddans of desert land, a significant expansion aimed at boosting food security and rural development. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to increase agricultural area and production through both horizontal land reclamation and vertical expansion utilizing scientific research and digital transformation. The goal is to maximize added value, achieve self-sufficiency, reduce the import gap, and provide safe food at affordable prices for citizens.

The minister highlighted major land reclamation projects including the New Delta (2.2 million feddans), Toshka (1.1 million feddans), North and Central Sinai (456,000 feddans), New Egyptian Rural Development (1.5 million feddans), and projects in South Upper Egypt and the New Valley (650,000 feddans). These efforts have transformed the agricultural sector, demonstrating the state's commitment to securing food and agricultural product needs, even as other nations faced challenges and imposed export restrictions.

Farouk emphasized that while the world loses agricultural land annually to desertification and climate change, Egypt has managed to expand its arable land. This proactive approach supports urban development and the agricultural sector, ensuring the nation's food supply. The "Egypt 2026 Forum" showcases this vision, with wide participation from society, political parties, and decision-makers, reflecting the government's focus on public policies and development programs.

eg.headline: Egypt president says military action to defend Saudi Arabia
eg.dek: President Al-Sisi stated Egypt's proposed military effort is solely for defending Saudi territory and not for attacking Yemen.
paragraphs: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi announced on Wednesday that any proposed Egyptian military effort would be directed towards defending Saudi Arabian territory, clarifying that it would not involve an attack on Yemen. He added that Egypt would extend this defense to any other Arab state upon request, emphasizing that the security of Gulf nations is integral to Egypt's own national security. Al-Sisi made these remarks during the Homeland and Citizen Security session at the Egypt Forum 2026, highlighting the indivisibility of Arab national security.

The President also addressed the importance of strengthening Egypt and maintaining public solidarity in the face of numerous risks, including the Ethiopian dam. He reiterated that targeting state institutions, as seen in 2011, is a tactic to destabilize nations. Al-Sisi identified the armed forces and the Interior Ministry as foundational pillars of state security, noting ongoing attempts to undermine the Interior Ministry's role and public perception.

Al-Sisi called for a review of the 2011 events to prevent their recurrence, citing the targeting of security forces, prison breaks, and subsequent consequences as examples of state collapse. He stressed the critical need to preserve state institutions, warning that their failure leads to widespread problems, a situation he noted is evident in the current regional landscape.

eg.headline: President asks developer for 200,000 rental homes
eg.dek: President el-Sisi urged businessman Hisham Talaat Moustafa to provide rental apartments as part of a large investment deal.
paragraphs: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi asked businessman Hisham Talaat Moustafa on Tuesday to help provide between 100,000 and 200,000 rental apartments. The request came during a session on urban development at the Egypt Forum 2026, following an agreement for Moustafa’s company, Talaat Moustafa Group, to develop four mixed-use projects with an investment of EGP 11 trillion. El-Sisi stated that developers undertaking projects of such scale should also contribute to society, questioning the social service aspect of major investments.

Moustafa responded affirmatively, citing the private sector’s contributions to social initiatives. However, el-Sisi clarified that this request was separate from existing programs like the Haya Karima initiative and the Long Live Egypt Fund. He emphasized the scale of his proposal by noting that 1 percent of the announced investment would equal EGP 100 billion.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly also spoke at the forum, announcing a major housing program that will include rental apartments, social housing, and projects for middle-income households. This initiative, to be rolled out over four years, aims to expand access to affordable housing across different income groups and revive rental housing as a key option.

eg.headline: Egypt forum highlights school attendance gains amid teacher shortages
eg.dek: Government officials presented improved school attendance as a success at the Egypt Forum 2026, despite ongoing concerns about teacher and classroom scarcity.
paragraphs: The Egypt Forum 2026, an event mandated by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, showcased a reported increase in school attendance as a key achievement in the nation's education sector. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly announced that basic education would anchor the forum's opening session, focusing on whether current curricula prepare students for future labor markets. The government framed this attendance boost as a transition point, allowing a shift in policy focus from expanding access to ensuring learning quality.

However, Mada Masr's investigation into the attendance claims suggests that increased regular testing, a recent curriculum change, is a significant driver of the reported gains. This innovation has drawn criticism from families and members of parliament who argue it strains students and teachers without improving educational outcomes, and potentially conflicts with pedagogical research.

Despite these criticisms and a general backdrop of chronic low spending in education, the government used the forum to highlight progress. The Education Minister outlined achievements, emphasizing the rise in school attendance as a foundation for future improvements in learning quality, a narrative presented amidst public inquiries and parliamentary pushback over recent ministry decisions.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea inflation hits 3.0% in September
gq.dek: Consumer prices rose across the country, with food, alcohol, transport, and health services seeing significant increases.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea recorded a 3.0% inflation rate in September 2026, surpassing the CEMAC threshold. The rise was driven by increases in several key sectors. Food and non-alcoholic beverages saw a 1.8% inflation, while alcoholic beverages and tobacco increased by 5.4%. Transport prices rose 3.6%, and health services experienced a 4.6% inflation rate. Restaurants and hotels saw a 2.7% price increase.

Within the food sector, significant price hikes were observed in coffee, tea, and cocoa (11.0%), fish (9.4%), zebu meat (11.0%), pastries (8.8%), and dairy products (14.1%). Alcoholic beverages and tobacco prices were pushed up by a 16.1% increase in spirits and a 5.9% rise in wines. Transport costs were affected by a 15.4% increase in car prices and a 5.7% rise in motorcycle prices.

Cities of Malabo and Ebibeyin registered the highest inflation rates at 4.9% each, both exceeding the community threshold. Evinayong recorded 2.7% inflation, Mongomo 1.6%, and Bata 1.1%. Overall, the general price level increased by seven tenths of a percent compared to the previous month.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea VP demands fuel distribution plan
gq.dek: The vice president has ordered Gepetrol to create a master plan within 48 hours to end the country's fuel crisis.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's vice president has demanded a comprehensive master plan from state oil company Gepetrol to resolve the ongoing fuel crisis. He described the current situation, with multiple distributors simultaneously lacking fuel, as an unacceptable systemic failure. The vice president has given Gepetrol 48 hours to present a definitive plan aimed at preventing future shortages.

The proposed strategy includes increasing fuel purchase volumes in the short term, reclaiming leased storage tanks, and constructing new, larger facilities to expand national reserves. In the long term, the government plans to build a national refinery to ensure domestic supply and serve partner countries in the subregion. The goal is to establish Gepetrol as the central hub for national fuel distribution, allowing both domestic companies and neighboring countries to purchase fuel directly.

To inform these decisions, Gepetrol and the Ministry of Mines will analyze five years of national fuel consumption data. The vice president also proposed exporting small quantities of crude oil for refining in neighboring countries to minimize costs and increase revenue. These measures aim to strengthen Gepetrol's capacity to manage crises and supply both domestic and regional partners.

gq.headline: Military personnel tortured and jailed amid leak accusations
gq.dek: 201 soldiers face detention and mistreatment in Black Beach prison following allegations of leaking sensitive information.
paragraphs: Sources within the Ministry of Defense have confirmed the detention of 201 military personnel accused of leaking sensitive information. Testimonies suggest these detentions involve coercive interrogations, leading to widespread unease within the armed forces. This operation is reportedly targeting soldiers from various branches, raising concerns about internal stability.

The accusations of leaking information are reportedly false, fueling fears that such claims are being used to target individuals who question the Ministry of Defense's operations and alleged corruption. The situation has created significant anxiety among military ranks, potentially fracturing the unity of the Equatorial Guinean Armed Forces.

The detained soldiers have been transferred to Black Beach prison, a facility known for its harsh conditions. The scale of the detentions and the alleged mistreatment highlight a severe internal security issue within the nation's military apparatus, with implications for its operational readiness and public trust.

Before her latest appointment, she directed the Press and Image Cabinet of the Vice Presidency since 2018, where she spearheaded institutional communication initiatives. She studied Political Science at the National University of Equatorial Guinea and has undertaken courses in image, presentation, and business management.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea reshuffles economic council members
gq.dek: Presidential decrees dismiss and appoint officials to the National Council for Economic and Social Development.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's President has issued decrees to change leadership within the National Council for Economic and Social Development (CNDES). Decree 126/2026 details the dismissal of several key figures, including members Bindang Ndong Okiri, Eduardo Orobiyi Lajay, and Teodora Ronda Rubio. The decree also removed Paulino Bololo Ekobo from his role as Counselor and Anacleto Nsue as Secretary General.

Following these dismissals, Decree 127/2026 announces the appointment of new officials to the CNDES. Seven new members have been named, including Anacleto Nsue Meñan Abegue and Paulino Bololo Ekobo, who were previously dismissed from different positions. Additionally, three new counselors were appointed, and 10 high-ranking officials, including a new Secretary General, Ismael Mercader Okenve, were designated to various technical and administrative roles.

The changes affect multiple levels of the CNDES, impacting its membership, advisory roles, and senior administrative functions. The newly appointed officials will oversee areas such as international relations, development agendas, social policies, industrial and environmental commissions, legal services, and budget execution. The specific reasons for the dismissals and appointments were not provided in the decrees.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: The removal of US sanctions, imposed for Eritrea's role in the Tigray War, may destabilize the opaque state by creating new openings for predatory officials.
paragraphs: The United States lifted sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026, ending measures imposed in 2021 due to the country's involvement in Ethiopia's Tigray War. Human rights groups have criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). The Eritrean government, however, welcomed the move, calling the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and arguing they hindered national development.

While Eritrea's government celebrates the removal of sanctions, observers suggest the benefits will likely accrue to the PFDJ's key financial and military apparatus, and two senior officials, rather than the impoverished population. The sanctions had targeted the ruling party's core structures, which are instrumental in maintaining control over political expression, capital flows, and national service conscripts. Past experience, following the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, indicates that the PFDJ's internal power dynamics are unlikely to change significantly.

The lifting of sanctions may create a paradoxically destabilizing effect within Eritrea, potentially empowering predatory officials seeking new political and economic opportunities. The PFDJ's strategy relies on repression to maintain control, and the removal of external constraints could exacerbate internal power struggles. Speculation also exists about a potential US-Eritrean partnership against Houthi forces in Yemen, following recent territorial gains by the Houthis.

ke.headline: Kenya plans tougher laws against illicit alcohol cartels
ke.dek: The government will introduce stricter legislation and boost enforcement to dismantle criminal networks involved in the production and sale of harmful alcoholic drinks.
paragraphs: Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has declared illicit alcohol a significant threat to Kenya’s future, vowing to implement tougher laws and intensify enforcement against production and sale networks. The government has elevated the fight against illicit brews and drug abuse, with a multi-agency response coordinated by the Deputy President's office. Kindiki stated that the alcohol menace could undermine national progress and emphasized a commitment to successful intervention, distinguishing the crackdown from targeting legitimate businesses.

The campaign involves agencies such as the National Authority for the Campaign Against Alcohol and Drug Abuse (NACADA), the Anti-Counterfeit Authority, the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS), and the Anti-Narcotics Unit. A permanent secretariat has been established at Harambee House Annex to coordinate ongoing enforcement and inter-agency collaboration. Law enforcement agencies are directed to support NACADA's operations, with the government expecting improved results from the intensified crackdown.

Recent coordinated efforts over 10 days led to nine successful raids on premises selling illicit ethanol and 116 raids targeting sellers of illicit brews nationwide. The government is also pursuing amendments to the legal framework governing the manufacture, distribution, and sale of alcoholic drinks to close loopholes exploited by criminal networks and impose tougher penalties.

ke.headline: Port of Lamu receives second Dangote refinery equipment shipment
ke.dek: The Port of Lamu received 154 pieces of heavy machinery for the proposed Dangote East Africa Refinery, marking progress on the KSh 2.2 trillion project.
paragraphs: The Port of Lamu has received a second shipment of equipment for the proposed Dangote East Africa Refinery. The MV Great Glory docked carrying 154 pieces of heavy machinery, following an earlier delivery in late September. The KSh 2.2 trillion (US$17 billion) refinery is designed to process up to 700,000 barrels of crude oil daily and is expected to become the largest refining complex in East Africa.

These successive shipments signify physical progress for the refinery project, which requires significant logistical capabilities that Lamu has demonstrated. The port's infrastructure, including its 17.5-meter berth depth, allows for direct discharge of heavy modules. The port handled nearly 800,000 metric tonnes in 2025 and plans to add 21 berths by 2030.

The refinery's construction phase is expected to generate substantial cargo volumes through Lamu over the next 40 months, supporting the port's expansion plans. The long-term viability will depend on sustained throughput after construction and securing crude supply arrangements to operate at design capacity.

ke.headline: Ex-official alleges procurement pressure in Sakaja fallout
ke.dek: Former Nairobi Chief Officer Geoffrey Mosiria claims Governor Sakaja sidelined him and pressured him into questionable procurement deals.
paragraphs: Former Nairobi County Chief Officer Geoffrey Mosiria has accused Governor Johnson Sakaja of sidelining him for nearly three years and pressuring him into questionable procurement deals. Mosiria stated that his powers as an accounting officer were effectively transferred to junior officers on December 28, 2023, through an unprocedural memo. He also alleged that his health budget was drastically reduced from Sh1.2 billion to Sh100 million, hindering his ability to perform duties.

Mosiria claimed the fallout began after he refused to participate in direct procurement arrangements that he believed would benefit individuals close to the governor and his contractors. He recounted a confrontation during a WhatsApp conference call with Chief of Staff Osman Khalifa regarding these procurement issues. Subsequently, Mosiria was transferred to the Environment department, where he felt he had little authority, and later to Public Participation, Citizen Engagement and Customer Service.

Despite facing alleged attacks in official groups, public criticism, and a court case for contempt, Mosiria stated he chose to lead enforcement operations on the streets to serve Nairobi residents. He also claimed to have received information about preparations for a court case intended to jail him, expressing his hope that Nairobians would discern who truly serves them and who belongs in jail.

ke.headline: KFC launches Kenyan-inspired food and entertainment campaign
ke.dek: The fast-food chain introduces a limited-time menu and retail activations with local creatives in Nairobi.
paragraphs: KFC has launched Kentucky Town 254, a Kenyan-inspired food and entertainment campaign running from October 20 to November 15, 2026. The initiative combines locally influenced menu innovations with retail activations and partnerships with Kenyan creatives. The campaign introduces a limited-time menu at selected KFC restaurants in Nairobi, featuring items like The Colonel’s Mandazi Burger, The Colonel’s Mandazi Pops, The Kentucky Choma Burger, Samosa Crunch, and Catch These Masala Fries, alongside new beverages.

The campaign extends beyond the menu with pop-up experiences at The Junction Mall, The Hub Karen, Galleria Shopping Mall, and Garden City Mall, featuring games, live performances, and music. A limited-edition merchandise collection, developed with Kenyan fashion and design brand JDHAA | home Apparel 254, is also part of the offering. KFC Africa stated that the initiative was developed around local creators, suppliers, and talent, with execution led in Kenya, which is its second-largest market in Africa with 48 restaurants.

This campaign reflects a localisation strategy adapting international quick-service restaurant offerings to regional tastes and creating opportunities to collaborate with local suppliers, designers, and entertainment talent. KFC Africa aims to build a restaurant brand that reflects African consumers, local partnerships, and regional creativity. The approach highlights the potential of limited-time menus to test new flavour combinations, generate customer engagement, and connect global brands with local food cultures.

ke.dek: Dr. Mukami Ruoro-Oundo recognized for her work treating injured and trafficked animals, strengthening conservation efforts.
paragraphs: Kenyan veterinary doctor Dr. Mukami Ruoro-Oundo has received international recognition, being named Wildlife Vet of the Year at the 2026 International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) Animal Action Awards in London. The Senior Veterinary Officer at the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) was honored on October 15, 2026, for her significant contributions to wildlife rescue, veterinary medicine, and conservation.

Dr. Mukami's work involves treating animals with severe injuries and life-threatening conditions, often in remote areas. Her patients have included elephants with fractured limbs, rhinos with infected wounds, lions caught in snares, and pangolins rescued from illegal trafficking. She develops specialised treatment protocols, particularly for pangolins, enhancing their survival rates after rescue from illegal trade.

Her expertise extends to managing complex cases with limited resources, requiring quick decision-making and extensive veterinary knowledge. Beyond individual animal care, Dr. Mukami's development of treatment procedures and sharing of professional knowledge are strengthening wildlife healthcare practices and supporting long-term conservation efforts across Kenya.

za.headline: Godongwana cuts fuel levy to offer relief
za.dek: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced a reduction in the fuel levy to provide temporary relief to South Africans from November 4.
paragraphs: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has reduced the fuel levy to offer relief to South Africans, announcing a cut of R3 per litre for diesel and R1.50 per litre for petrol. This temporary measure will be in effect from November 4, 2026, until December 1, 2026. Following this initial reduction, a lower amount of relief will continue until January 5, 2027, with the diesel levy reduced by R1.50 per litre and the petrol levy by R1 per litre.

The announcement came as Godongwana delivered his medium-term budget policy statement on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. The National Treasury has also lowered growth forecasts and warned of short-lived revenue gains, while introducing R10 billion in temporary fuel relief to ease household pressure. Opposition parties have dismissed the cuts as electioneering, though the GNU offered muted support.

The decision aims to ease household pressure amid economic concerns. While the full impact on government revenue is yet to be determined, the relief is intended to provide immediate financial respite for consumers facing rising costs. The duration and scale of the cuts reflect a balance between offering support and managing fiscal implications.

za.headline: Swimmer killed in shark attack at Orient Beach
za.dek: A 65-year-old woman died after a shark attack while swimming at Orient Beach, leading to the closure of local beaches.
paragraphs: A fatal shark attack occurred at Orient Beach in KuGompo City on Tuesday morning, claiming the life of 65-year-old Janine Lochrenberg. Lochrenberg, a retired nuclear radiographer and musician, was open water swimming with a group when she was attacked. She sustained severe injuries to her right arm and leg and was declared dead at the scene by a medic from the swimming group. Police have opened an investigation into the incident.

Following the attack, Orient Beach and Eastern Beach were closed until further notice by the Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality. Municipal spokesman Luzuko Buku confirmed the tragic loss of a swimmer. Fellow swimmer Mike Loewe, who was in the water at the time, recounted that members of their open-water swimming group responded to Lochrenberg's distress signal and brought her ashore. Loewe described Lochrenberg as courageous and someone who liked to swim solo.

Tributes have poured in for Lochrenberg from across South Africa and her swimming community. East London Open Water Swimming described her as a treasured member whose loss leaves an enormous hole in their ocean family. They remembered her as someone who quietly did what she loved most, finding joy in the ocean, and being a vital part of the heart of their group.
