za.headline: Kaizer Chiefs seek CAF Confederation Cup win at home
za.dek: The South African club must overcome a first-leg deficit against Red Arrows to advance to the group stages of the continental competition.
paragraphs: Kaizer Chiefs face Red Arrows on Friday evening in the second leg of their CAF Confederation Cup tie, needing to overturn a 1-0 loss from the first match in Zambia. Failure to win by at least two clear goals will result in their elimination from the competition. Coach Fernando Da Cruz is expected to deploy an attacking formation to put immediate pressure on the visitors.

The predicted starting lineup includes Renaldo Leaner in goal, with Reeve Frosler at right-back due to Thabiso Monyane's injury. Miguel Ignacio and Thabo Moloisane are set to form the central defense, and Bradley Cross will play left-back. In midfield, Sibongiseni Mthethwa and Lebohang Maboe are expected to provide balance, while Mduduzi Vilakazi will operate as an attacking midfielder.

The forward line is anticipated to feature Pule Mmodi on the left wing, Duba on the right, and Flavio Silva as the lone striker. Kaizer Chiefs will rely on their attackers to convert chances and secure a home victory to progress to the CAF Confederation Cup group stages.

za.headline: Media wins sight of SSA secrecy application in R12 million fraud trial
za.dek: News organisations have obtained a redacted copy of the State Security Agency’s application to close the corruption trial of two former senior officials.
paragraphs: Several South African media organisations have obtained a redacted copy of the State Security Agency’s (SSA) application to close the corruption trial of two former senior officials, Patrick Mshothola and Thulani Dlomo. The SSA is seeking a total ban on media and public access to the remaining proceedings, citing risks to intelligence sources and methods. The Mail & Guardian, Media24, amaBhungane, Daily Maverick, and the Campaign for Free Expression were among the outlets that secured the document.

Mshothola and Dlomo, who led the SSA’s special operations directorate between 2012 and 2017, face charges of theft, fraud, forgery, and uttering involving approximately R12 million. They were arrested on November 30, 2025, marking the first prosecution of SSA personnel stemming from the High Level Review Panel and the Zondo Commission. The trial commenced in the Pretoria High Court on October 12, 2026.

The court had previously ordered restrictions on public access, including closed proceedings for evidence related to SSA members, operational methods, and classified documents, following the State’s section 153(1) application on October 14, 2026. This was done without prior notice to the media or the public. The Mail & Guardian intervened as a co-applicant, seeking access to the sealed record and any future sealed documents.

za.headline: Mabandla denies halting TRC prosecutions
za.dek: Former justice minister Brigitte Mabandla told the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry she did not instruct a moratorium on post-TRC cases.
paragraphs: Former justice minister Brigitte Mabandla has denied instructing a halt to prosecutions related to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC). Testifying before the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry on Wednesday, Mabandla stated she never made a phone call on November 11, 2004, to National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) senior official Dr Silas Ramaite, requesting a moratorium on TRC cases.

Ramaite, who oversaw TRC prosecutions and acted as head of the NPA, had previously alleged that Mabandla informed him of an "outside mechanism" and a declared "moratorium" on post-TRC prosecutions. He claimed this instruction led him to direct advocate Anton Ackermann to put investigations on hold, specifically mentioning the attempted murder of Reverend Frank Chikane in 1989 as a case potentially affected.

Mabandla asserted that neither she nor any official from her ministry issued such an instruction to Ramaite. She expressed her determination to uncover the truth, stating she had consulted with former NPA head Vusi Pikoli to clarify her certainty that the alleged phone call could not have occurred.

ng.headline: Nigeria confirms Ebola Bundibugyo strain
ng.dek: The World Health Organisation stated that the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, confirmed in Nigeria's capital, has no vaccine or specific treatment.
paragraphs: Nigeria has confirmed its first case of the Ebola virus, identified as the Bundibugyo strain, in the Federal Capital Territory. The patient, a woman, arrived in Abuja on October 3 via Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333 from Uganda. She received care at a private hospital before diagnosis and has since been moved to an isolation facility. The World Health Organisation has stated that this strain of the virus has no vaccine or specific treatment.

Health authorities have initiated extensive contact-tracing efforts, identifying 44 close contacts including healthcare workers, patients, and caregivers. The Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units nationwide on high alert. Uganda has requested detailed travel and clinical records from Nigeria, asserting the patient did not contract the virus within its territory as there are no current Ebola cases there.

The National Assembly has urged the Federal Government to release emergency funds to relevant agencies to combat the disease and to make passenger screening mandatory at all entry points and borders. They also called for an immediate amendment to the Quarantine Act of 1926. Health officials are urging the public to remain calm and follow advice from health authorities.

ng.headline: Standard Chartered names Adelagun CEO
ng.dek: Ayodeji Adelagun has been confirmed as the new Chief Executive Officer of Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited after serving as acting CEO since January.
paragraphs: Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited has confirmed Ayodeji Adelagun as its Chief Executive Officer following regulatory approval by the Central Bank of Nigeria. Adelagun, who has over 26 years of banking experience in Africa, has been acting CEO since January 2026. He previously held senior roles at the bank, including Head of Markets for Nigeria and Africa, and Head of Rates and Credit Trading for West Africa.

Adelagun stated that Nigeria remains a significant long-term growth market for Standard Chartered, with an ambition to deliver greater value for clients and the economy. His focus will be on deepening client relationships, driving sustainable growth, and leveraging the bank's international network for Nigerian clients. He is also Chairman of Standard Chartered Capital and Advisory Nigeria.

A Fellow of the Financial Markets Dealers Association, Adelagun was instrumental in introducing benchmark bonds in Nigeria, which supported the country's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Markets Index. He also pioneered bond trading desks at FSDH and Standard Chartered Bank and previously worked in various roles at Access Bank Plc.

ng.headline: Comedian Broda Shaggi recounts stray bullet injury
ng.dek: Nollywood actor Samuel Perry, known as Broda Shaggi, described his fear and uncertainty after being shot by a stray bullet while filming a skit.
paragraphs: Nollywood actor and comedian Samuel Perry, known as Broda Shaggi, has detailed his recovery from a stray bullet injury that halted his career for months. The incident occurred while he was filming a comedy skit under the Sango-Ota bridge. Perry recounted being overwhelmed by fear, seeing blood, and praying for survival until he received first aid at a hospital. He expressed concern about his ability to continue performing, as dancing and physical activity are integral to his work.

The injury led Perry to worry about his future in entertainment and whether fans would forget him during his absence. He underwent surgery in Nigeria and later sought further treatment and physiotherapy in Dubai, where his recovery progressed rapidly. Perry stated he could stand with support two days after the Dubai operation and walk with crutches by the third day, describing his survival as a second chance.

Perry, who had maintained a demanding work schedule since 2018, feared his prolonged absence would lead to public amnesia. He is now able to stand without crutches but still uses them for support. The comedian expressed gratitude for being alive and promised fans new projects, urging them to anticipate his return to their screens with exciting content.

et.headline: Ethiopian park signs avocado processing deal with diaspora investor
et.dek: The Sidama Industrial Parks Development Corporation will host a new facility expected to process 150 tonnes of avocados daily for export.
paragraphs: The Sidama Industrial Parks Development Corporation has signed an investment agreement with Basilea Trading One Member PLC to establish an avocado-processing facility at the Yirgalem Integrated Agro-Industrial Park. The project, led by diaspora investor Bekalu Getahun, has completed its preparatory requirements and entered the implementation phase. Once operational, the facility is expected to process up to 150 tonnes of raw avocados per day, with plans to export up to six containers of processed products to international markets each month.

Avocado processing converts raw fruit into products with longer shelf life and higher value, such as pulp, refined oil for cooking and cosmetics, and animal feed from by-products. This value-addition model captures more value from the fruit and reduces waste. The project's viability hinges on securing raw materials through agreements with local growers, potentially requiring aggregation through cooperatives or contract farming to ensure consistent daily volumes.

The facility adds an anchor tenant to Yirgalem Park, potentially attracting related investment in cold storage, packaging, and transport infrastructure. The corporation plans further expansion into refined avocado oil, cosmetics, and animal feed production. The employment impact spans permanent roles in processing and logistics, and temporary positions during harvest seasons.

et.headline: Ethiopian PM honours Kenyan heroes
et.dek: Abiy Ahmed attended Eldoret's Mashujaa Day celebrations, noting shared history and unity between the nations.
paragraphs: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed attended Kenya's Mashujaa Day celebrations in Eldoret on Tuesday, October 20. He paid tribute to the nation's freedom fighters and national heroes. Ahmed highlighted the shared history of struggle, sacrifice, and national unity between Ethiopia and Kenya.

During his address at the event, Prime Minister Ahmed lauded the bravery of Kenyans. He emphasized the common bonds that tie the two East African nations together. The celebration served as a platform to acknowledge the contributions of those who fought for Kenya's independence and national identity.

The presence of the Ethiopian Prime Minister underscored the strong diplomatic ties and mutual respect between the two countries. Mashujaa Day, meaning 'Heroes' Day', is a public holiday in Kenya dedicated to remembering and honouring all those who contributed to the nation's progress.

gh.headline: Ghana's National Investment Bank returns to profit
gh.dek: The bank's capital adequacy ratio rose to 23% after a government cash injection and bond offering.
paragraphs: Ghana's National Investment Bank (NIB) has reported a profit after tax of GH¢343.9 million for the 2025 financial year, a significant turnaround from GH¢2.7 million in 2024. This recovery follows a GH¢450 million cash injection, GH¢1.5 billion in re-marketable bonds, and the transfer of GH¢500 million in government-held Nestlé Ghana shares. The interventions pushed NIB's capital adequacy ratio to approximately 23% by May 2025, from a negative level as low as -53.13% at the end of 2024.

The Finance Ministry stated that these measures protected GH¢6.4 billion in depositor funds and preserved over 900 jobs, contrasting with the widespread job losses and institutional collapses during the 2017-2019 banking sector clean-up. During that period, 420 financial institutions failed, costing over 10,000 jobs and requiring GH¢25 billion in government spending.

NIB's financial performance in 2025 showed total assets more than doubling to GH¢12.22 billion from GH¢5.84 million in 2024. Customer deposits increased to GH¢10.20 billion from GH¢6.47 billion, while loans and advances grew to GH¢730 million from GH¢670 million. Total equity climbed to GH¢1.55 billion.

gh.headline: Ghana targets AI facility within 24 months
gh.dek: The government aims to complete the first phase of a national computing facility to boost local artificial intelligence development.
paragraphs: Ghana plans to complete the initial phase of a national computing facility within two years, providing local researchers, universities, and businesses with essential computing power for artificial intelligence (AI) development. The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, stated that procurement processes are underway with the Public Procurement Authority for the necessary data centre infrastructure and equipment. This facility is intended to reduce the current reliance on external computing services purchased by Ghanaian entities.

The planned facility will offer computing resources crucial for AI research and commercial applications, which often demand significant processing power for model training, application execution, and large-scale data analysis. Minister George described the project as a foundational step towards positioning Ghana to actively participate in the evolving AI economy. He cautioned that this facility represents an initial milestone rather than a complete solution to the nation's AI infrastructure needs.

The government's 24-month target outlines the timeline for the first phase of the computing facility. Further investment and consistent policy implementation will be necessary to achieve Ghana's broader AI ambitions. The success of the facility will depend on its capacity, affordability, reliability, and accessibility to its intended users, including researchers, universities, and businesses working with AI technologies.

gh.headline: Analyst urges Ghana to boost farm extension services
gh.dek: Dr Joseph Opoku Gakpo says stronger support for agricultural extension personnel is essential to improving food security and farmer innovation.
paragraphs: Agricultural analyst Dr Joseph Opoku Gakpo has called on the Ghanaian government to prioritize agricultural extension services, stating that enhanced support for these personnel is crucial for helping farmers adopt new technologies and ultimately improving national food security. He emphasized that investments in agricultural research will yield limited benefits if farmers do not receive clear communication about innovations and cannot implement them effectively.

Dr Gakpo highlighted that effective extension services act as a vital link between research institutions and farming practices. He noted that without adequate investment in extension personnel and their supporting systems, innovations developed in universities and research centers may not reach the farmers who need them. This gap limits the potential benefits of agricultural research investments, hindering the adoption of practices like regenerative farming or improved post-harvest techniques.

The analyst stressed that extension workers require not only technical knowledge in areas such as crop and livestock production, soil health, and pest management but also strong communication and interpersonal skills. Building trust with farmers is paramount for the successful introduction of new technologies, as demonstrated by research co-authored by Dr Gakpo, which identified trust as a key factor in technology acceptance among Ghanaian farmers.

gh.headline: IMF mission reviews Ghana's 2027 budget plans
gh.dek: Discussions will focus on fiscal performance, revenue, inflation, and debt as Ghana seeks to consolidate economic gains.
paragraphs: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission began formal engagements with the Ghanaian government today to review the country's fiscal performance, revenue mobilization, and preparations for the 2027 Budget. Sources familiar with the visit indicate the discussions will cover economic performance for the first nine months of the year, necessary policies to maintain recent gains, and Ghana's debt position. Expenditure management for the remainder of the current year and spending plans for 2027, with a focus on infrastructure investment, are also on the agenda.

The mission will also examine Ghana's inflation-targeting framework, monetary policy, and foreign exchange arrangements. Potential assessments of the Bank of Ghana's financial standing, international reserves, and measures to protect the central bank's independence are expected. Initial discussions involve officials from the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Ghana, with other economic stakeholders anticipated to join the two-week visit.

This mission is part of Ghana's engagement under the Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI), a non-financing framework designed to consolidate economic gains and sustain policy reforms. The PCI, which does not provide direct IMF funding, allows the government to demonstrate progress on policy commitments and bolster confidence among investors and development partners. Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson has described the framework as crucial for strengthening economic resilience and supporting broad-based growth.

cd.headline: Lawmaker announces no-confidence vote against agriculture minister
cd.dek: A national lawmaker plans to introduce a motion of no-confidence against the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security over alleged embezzlement of $57 million.
paragraphs: National Assembly member Hermione Bolumbe announced on October 21, 2026, that she will soon file a motion of no-confidence against Muhindo Nzangi, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security. The motion is based on suspicions of embezzlement totaling $57 million.

The announcement comes amid broader discussions in Congolese media about the country's security and political crises. Other headlines on October 22, 2026, included calls for peace from the LUCHA movement directed at former president Joseph Kabila and current president Félix Tshisekedi, as well as statements from Belgium regarding the FRN and threats made by Fils Mukoko.

The specific allegations against Minister Nzangi have not yet been detailed in public reports. The motion, if filed and passed, could lead to the minister's removal from office and potentially trigger a cabinet reshuffle.

cd.headline: Nurses' strike leaves 60 patients without care in DR Congo
cd.dek: Around 60 patients at Onema Ototo hospital in Sankuru are not receiving treatment after nurses began a strike over pay and risk bonuses.
paragraphs: Around 60 patients at the Onema Ototo general reference hospital in the Sankuru province are without care following a nurses' strike that began last week. The nurses are demanding administrative and financial support from the government, along with payment of their risk premiums. Patients previously in various wards are now consolidated in one pavilion due to the lack of nursing staff.

Patients who underwent surgery before the strike reported that their wounds are not being dressed and they are not receiving injections. One patient described the situation as precarious, with surgical wounds unmaintained and a lack of essential medical care, urging authorities to intervene. The head of the Ototo health zone, Dr. Mathieu Lotshilenge, confirmed that the zone faces a shortage of medical personnel and administrative and financial difficulties.

Dr. Lotshilenge stated that the health zone has only three doctors, with one on leave. Of the remaining two, only he receives a premium but is not salaried, while the rest of the staff are neither salaried nor receive premiums. The approximately 60 patients remain in precarious conditions at the hospital, awaiting a government response to the healthcare workers' demands to resume medical services.

cd.headline: Kolwezi protests leave two injured and property damaged
cd.dek: Artisanal miners demonstrated for two days in Kolwezi, paralyzing economic activity and causing injuries and material damage.
paragraphs: A gradual calm returned to several neighborhoods in Kolwezi, Lualaba province, on Wednesday, October 21, following two days of violent demonstrations by artisanal miners. Local sources reported that the unrest disrupted socio-economic activities and resulted in several injuries and significant material damage.

The protests, which lasted for two days, brought normal life to a standstill in the affected areas. The scale of the material damage is still being assessed, but initial reports indicate it is substantial. The number of injured has been confirmed by local sources, though specific details about their conditions were not immediately available.

The demonstrations by artisanal miners have had a direct impact on the local economy, halting daily business and trade. The return to calm suggests a de-escalation of the situation, though the full extent of the consequences of the two-day unrest is yet to be determined.

cd.headline: DR Congo official banned from media over threats
cd.dek: Fils Mukoko, an official of the ruling UDPS party, faces media ban and judicial inquiry for inciting violence against Western nationals.
paragraphs: Congolese authorities have reacted strongly to controversial statements made by Fils Mukoko, a cadre of the UDPS party. Mukoko allegedly posted threats on social media to arm youth against Western nationals following searches of residences near the presidential family. In response, the Superior Council of Audiovisual and Communication (CSAC) banned Mukoko from all media and social networks for 88 days, citing violations of human life sanctity and respect for diplomatic missions.

Mukoko has also been removed from his position as deputy director general of the Kinshasa Sanitation Authority (RASKIN) by the city's governor. The Ministry of Justice has initiated a judicial investigation, with the Minister of State for Justice instructing the prosecutor general to examine allegations that Mukoko spoke of distributing weapons and threatening Western residents.

The government stated that the gravity of Mukoko's declarations warrants rigorous verification by judicial authorities. The Ministry emphasized that freedom of expression does not justify threats, intimidation, or statements endangering others' lives, regardless of constitutional guarantees.

cd.headline: DR Congo students receive school supplies after floods
cd.dek: Nearly 500 students in Luiza, Kasaï-Central, received stationery to continue their studies after heavy rains destroyed their belongings.
paragraphs: 490 students in Luiza, Kasaï-Central province, have received school supplies following torrential rains on September 27. The local community mobilized to provide this assistance, aiming to ensure the children can resume their education despite the damage caused by the severe weather.

The initiative addresses the immediate needs of students whose learning materials were lost or damaged. This support is crucial for maintaining educational continuity in the affected region, where many families are still awaiting aid.

More than a thousand households in Luiza were also impacted by the floods, and they are still in need of further assistance. The distribution of school supplies marks a first step in helping the community recover from the disaster.

tz.headline: Tanzania fish exports rise 11.3% to US$181.6M
tz.dek: The East African nation's seafood earnings grew due to investments in processing, preservation, and logistics, boosting international competitiveness.
paragraphs: Tanzania's fish exports reached US$181.6 million in the year ending August 2026, an 11.3% increase from US$163.1 million the previous year. This growth, attributed to improvements in processing, preservation, and logistics, highlights the impact of investments in seafood processing, cold storage, and export infrastructure. The Bank of Tanzania reported the US$18.5 million rise, underscoring efforts to strengthen the country's position in global markets.

Lake Victoria contributes an estimated 80% to 85% of Tanzania's annual fish exports, which range between 57,000 and 60,000 tonnes. Nile perch fillets are a primary export, supplying markets in Europe, the Americas, and Asia. Sardines from Lakes Victoria and Tanganyika, along with fish maws sent to China and Hong Kong, also contribute to export earnings. The United States, the European Union, and other African nations are also key export destinations.

Initiatives like the Fish4ACP project are enhancing processing capabilities and reducing post-harvest losses. Improved smoking kilns and energy-efficient stoves minimize smoke exposure and contamination, while solar-powered freezers and new ice plants in Kigoma and Uvinza, with a capacity of 15 tonnes daily, are cutting production costs by 50%. Training in marketing, financial literacy, and fisheries regulation further supports the sector's development.

tz.headline: Tanzania launches digital library system
tz.dek: Education Minister Adolf Mkenda urged the Tanzania Library Services Board to prioritise books over new buildings.
paragraphs: Tanzania has launched its Integrated National Digital Library System, known as iNDLS, a platform designed to consolidate member registration, ISBN/ISSN applications, cataloguing, and lending management. Education Minister Adolf Mkenda officially inaugurated the system, developed by the library board in collaboration with the e-Government Authority, at the National Library in Dar es Salaam. The digital service aims to broaden access to publications and library information via web browsers and a mobile application, though copyright restrictions may limit full online availability of some titles.

During the launch, Mkenda advised the Tanzania Library Services Board to shift funding from constructing new library facilities towards acquiring and distributing books. He stressed the importance of repairing existing infrastructure while prioritising the purchase of local titles to support writers and publishers and expand reading access. The minister also encouraged local authorities and organisations to establish small public libraries, with the board providing the necessary books.

The initiative addresses long-standing challenges in book access in Tanzania, where, according to a 2025 UNESCO report, there was one bookshop for every 116,000 people and one public library for every 189,000 people. The ministry also plans to explore centralised subscriptions for online academic resources to reduce costs for universities and ensure transparent administration of government support for publishing, focusing on publishers with proven track records.

tz.headline: Tanzania joins SADC summit on regional governance
tz.dek: The nation participated in a virtual meeting to bolster solidarity, integration, and security cooperation among member states.
paragraphs: Tanzania has joined Southern African Development Community (SADC) member states in efforts to strengthen regional governance, solidarity, and integration. The nation participated in an Extraordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government held virtually on October 21, 2026. Ambassador Dr. Samwel William Shelukindo, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation, represented Tanzania at the meeting.

Leaders at the summit discussed key issues related to the governance and institutional operations of the regional bloc. The meeting was convened to approve the appointment of the SADC Deputy Executive Secretary for Regional Integration and to elect the incoming Chairperson of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation.

These measures are part of SADC’s broader efforts to enhance governance structures and cooperation among member states, particularly concerning peace and security. The initiative aims to foster a conducive environment for deeper regional integration and sustainable development across Southern Africa.

tz.dek: The Deputy Minister for Energy Salome Makamba submitted the first quarter budget implementation report for the 2026/27 financial year to the Parliamentary Standing Committee.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Energy presented its budget implementation report for the first quarter of the 2026/27 financial year to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Energy and Minerals in Dodoma. Deputy Minister Salome Makamba led the presentation, which covered progress in electricity and renewable energy subsectors, including research, production, and utilization of renewable energy sources.

The report detailed the implementation status of key projects such as the Second Phase of the Electricity Supply Project for Hamlets (HEP IIA and HEP IIB), the Strong Grid Project, and clean cooking energy initiatives. Budget implementation reports for the Tanzania Electric Supply Company Limited (TANESCO) and the Rural Energy Agency (REA) were also presented.

The meeting, chaired by Subira Mgalu, was attended by members of the parliamentary committee, Permanent Secretary Engineer Felshesmi Mramba, and the Managing Directors of TANESCO and REA, Lazaro Twange and Engineer Hassan Saidy, respectively. The session reviewed activities and budget execution in the electricity and renewable energy sectors during the initial quarter.

tz.headline: Tanzania bank and tech firm launch farming loans for youth
tz.dek: Azania Bank and Dronlytics offer financing for young farmers to adopt solar irrigation technology and expand operations.
paragraphs: Dronlytics Technologies Tanzania Limited and Azania Bank Plc have partnered to provide a dedicated agricultural loan facility for small-scale and youth farmers in Morogoro. This initiative aims to enable experienced young farmers, participating in the Dronlytics Block Farm Program, to transition to commercial-scale farming. The program supports the government's Building a Better Tomorrow: Youth Initiative for Agribusiness by offering a clear progression path for youth who have gained practical farming experience, with the first cohort expected in early 2027.

The collaboration combines Azania Bank's expertise in agricultural finance with Dronlytics' modern farming solutions, notably a USA-patented solar irrigation system designed to increase crop yields. This technology allows for up to three harvests annually, independent of seasonal rainfall, by precisely delivering water and inputs to crops. A University of Arkansas study showed similar systems reduced water use by 67% and fertilizer use by 30%, while also decreasing methane emissions from fields.

Farmers will own their irrigation systems, financed through Azania Bank and supported by Dronlytics' warranty. The program also includes drone scouting and a technology platform that integrates field and satellite data for precision agriculture. This integrated approach, from seed to market, with centralized services and mechanization, allows farmers to manage larger areas and concentrate on business development.

ma.headline: Morocco's Mansouri defends new government structure
ma.dek: The head of government addressed parliament, explaining decisions on ministerial appointments and budget deadlines.
paragraphs: Head of government Fatima Zahra Mansouri defended her new administration before the House of Councillors on October 21, addressing accusations of disorder and continuity with the previous government. She explained the dismissal of vocational training minister Madiha Khayr, stating that concerns about Khayr's past emerged only after her appointment. Mansouri requested Khayr's dismissal from King Mohammed VI, who approved it, citing difficulties in overseeing public funds.

Mansouri also defended the government's decision to approve and submit the draft 2027 Finance Bill before securing parliamentary confidence, emphasizing the need to meet the October 20 statutory deadline. She described this as an achievement that prevented financial year delays, though constitutional experts have raised disagreements about the legality of proceeding before investiture.

Furthermore, Mansouri rejected claims that her government was merely a continuation of the previous one led by Aziz Akhannouch. She dismissed the National Rally of Independents' accusation that her coalition reproduced past policies without a distinct agenda, stating that her government was formed around shared political choices. She also explained that rural development was moved from the Agriculture Ministry due to the failure of previous programs to yield expected improvements for rural residents.

ma.headline: Morocco divorce cases rise 4.38% in 2025
ma.dek: Total divorce and judicial separation filings reached 154,377, reversing a slight decline from the previous year, according to judicial data.
paragraphs: Morocco recorded 154,377 divorce and judicial separation cases in 2025, a 4.38% increase from the prior year. This rise follows a small decrease in 2024, when filings dropped to 147,895 from 151,168 in 2023. The Supreme Council of the Judicial Power's annual report, published in the Official Gazette, indicates that consensual divorce and judicial separation due to marital discord remain the most common reasons for ending marriages.

Divorce cases saw a slight uptick in 2024 to 40,212 from 40,028, and further increased by 1,252 cases in 2025. Judicial separation filings, however, experienced a decline in 2024 to 107,681 from 111,140, before rising by 5,230 cases to 112,911 in 2025. Consensual divorce constituted nearly 97% of all divorce cases throughout the three-year period analyzed.

The prevalence of consensual divorce is attributed to procedural flexibility and mutual agreement between spouses, which can mitigate conflict and reduce negative consequences for families. Judicial separation based on marital discord, known as shiqaq, accounted for the majority of judicial separation cases. The report distinguishes divorce as a dissolution of the marital bond and judicial separation as a court-ordered dissolution based on specified grounds.

ma.headline: Africa Eco Race to cross Morocco's southern provinces in January
ma.dek: The 18th edition of the rally will start in Tangier and pass through Laayoune and Dakhla before entering Mauritania, following past disruptions.
paragraphs: Organizers of the Africa Eco Race have announced the route for the rally's 18th edition, scheduled to begin on January 24, 2027. Competitors will travel from Tangier through several Moroccan cities, including Meknes, Erfoud, M’Hamid, Assa, Laayoune, and Dakhla, before crossing into Mauritania at Guerguerat. The race, which combines off-road racing with long-distance navigation, will conclude on February 6 near Dakar, Senegal. Organizers are planning to enhance logistical and safety measures along the route.

The passage through Morocco's southern provinces has previously faced objections from the Polisario Front. In 2020, demonstrators briefly obstructed the rally at Guerguerat, though participants were allowed to continue. This incident occurred before a wider blockade of the road later that year. The movement had previously warned organizers about risks in the Sahara, but the 2022 rally proceeded without reported security issues.

The Africa Eco Race, created in 2009, revived the traditional African route for the rally after the Dakar Rally relocated. Morocco, Mauritania, and Senegal have been key locations for the competition. The 2021 edition was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and severe weather conditions led to the cancellation of the opening stages in January 2026. Tangier will host the start for the second consecutive year in 2027.

ma.headline: Morocco beat Angola 5-2 to win fourth Futsal AFCON title
ma.dek: The Atlas Lions secured their fourth consecutive continental championship by defeating Angola in the final on home soil.
paragraphs: Morocco clinched their fourth consecutive Futsal Africa Cup of Nations title on Wednesday, beating Angola 5-2 in the final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Sports Hall in Rabat. Hicham Dguig’s team extended their continental dominance with a victory that saw them score three second-half goals.

Othmane El Idrissi opened the scoring for Morocco, but Joao Cambangula equalized for Angola. Youssef Jouad restored the hosts’ advantage before halftime. After the break, Idriss Raiss El Fenni, Ismail Amazal, and Bilal Bakkali added to the score, while Fortes Anderson netted Angola’s second goal.

This triumph marks Morocco's fourth consecutive African championship, following wins in 2016, 2020, and 2024. The team, coached by Dguig throughout this period, has established a commanding record in African futsal.

ma.headline: Boy, 11, found dead as Ziz river levels rise
ma.dek: Rescue teams recovered the body of an 11-year-old boy swept away by the swollen Ziz River in Erfoud, Morocco, following heavy rainfall.
paragraphs: Rescue teams recovered the body of an 11-year-old boy on Wednesday after he was swept away by the swollen Ziz River in Erfoud, southeastern Morocco. The child disappeared around 6 p.m. Tuesday, prompting a search involving local authorities and Civil Protection personnel. Specialist divers later joined the operation, with local outlets reporting his body was found Wednesday evening, roughly 24 hours after he went missing.

The incident occurs as rising water levels have prompted warnings across the Drâa-Tafilalet region, where the Guir-Ziz-Ghris Basin Agency activated flood-monitoring and early-warning stations on October 18. The agency urged residents to avoid riverbeds and refrain from crossing waterways as increased runoff moved through the region’s river network. Water levels have also risen sharply at Hassan Addakhil Dam near Errachidia, where the reservoir’s filling rate increased from 65.04% on October 19 to 71.99% the following day.

Authorities have continued urging caution around swollen rivers and low-lying crossings, where rapidly moving water can remain dangerous even after rainfall subsides. The latest incident follows several days of heightened flood monitoring in southeastern Morocco, with the condition of roads and communities along the Ziz River still requiring assessment.

ug.headline: Ugandans urged to cut travel as fuel prices climb
ug.dek: Petrol and diesel prices have risen sharply, increasing costs for essential goods and straining household budgets.
paragraphs: Ugandans are advised to reduce non-essential travel and opt for public transport due to soaring fuel prices. Petrol is now approximately Shs 6,800 per litre, with diesel at about Shs 7,000, according to Deputy Secretary to the Treasury Patrick Ocailap. These price hikes are expected to make food, transport, and other necessities more expensive for households already facing budget challenges.

Ocailap attributed the fuel price increases primarily to global market developments and exchange rate pressures. He noted that international oil prices have risen from about $59 to $104 a barrel since the start of a recent war. As Uganda imports fuel, higher global prices directly increase import costs, with a weakening shilling further exacerbating expenses.

The government stated that fuel taxes, with a Shs 200 increase on petrol tax this financial year bringing it to Shs 1,750 per litre, help fund public programs like the Parish Development Model. Ocailap rejected claims that domestic taxes or the proposed Sovereignty Bill were the main drivers of the price surge, emphasizing global factors and the need to buy imported fuel.

ug.headline: Uganda urged to turn research into food security solutions
ug.dek: Officials called for greater investment in agricultural innovation and adoption of research-based technologies to strengthen food security and improve nutrition.
paragraphs: Uganda's agricultural sector is facing significant challenges, including food insecurity, climate pressures, pests, diseases, and food contamination, according to officials and development partners. During World Food Day celebrations in Mbarara City, a strong call was made to move agricultural research out of laboratories and into the hands of farmers. The focus is on ensuring that innovations are accessible and usable to boost production, enhance resilience to changing weather patterns, and improve household incomes.

Minister Tumwebaze specifically urged agricultural extension workers to help farmers understand and implement practices that can improve their resilience to changing weather. The Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations highlighted that despite advances in agricultural science, hunger remains a global challenge, with millions facing food insecurity and unaffordability of healthy diets. The FAO stressed that scientific advances must translate into practical improvements for people's lives.

Innovations such as digital advisory services, early-warning systems, and improved farming practices can significantly help farmers increase production and adapt to climate change. However, their impact is limited when confined to research institutions. The FAO advocates for stronger cooperation among governments, researchers, businesses, and farming communities to make agricultural innovations accessible, affordable, and suited to local needs, contributing to better production, nutrition, environment, and life for all.

zw.headline: Bard Santner appoints international board for diaspora banking
zw.dek: The microfinance bank has appointed a 13-member board with former executives from major financial institutions to oversee its strategy.
paragraphs: Microfinance bank Bard Santner has launched a new 13-member board, including former executives from HSBC, KPMG, and PwC. The institution is specifically targeting Zimbabwe's diaspora remittances with its new banking strategy.

The board's primary objective is to provide strong corporate governance oversight and safeguard depositors' funds. This initiative comes in response to significant losses, totaling hundreds of millions of dollars, previously experienced by individuals due to mismanagement and economic instability.
Bard Santner aims to leverage the expertise of its international board members to navigate the complexities of the Zimbabwean market and rebuild confidence among investors and account holders.

cv.headline: Cape Verde tourist prices rise 7.5% year-on-year
cv.dek: Hotels, cafes, and restaurants saw the largest price increases in the third quarter, according to the National Statistics Institute.
paragraphs: Tourist prices in Cape Verde increased by 7.5% in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, the National Statistics Institute (INE) announced. The Tourist Price Index (IPT) showed that prices for hotels, cafes, and restaurants rose by 7.5%, while car rentals became 6.4% more expensive. Entertainment and culture services saw no price variation.

The INE's findings also revealed a 5.2% quarterly price increase between July and September, a significant jump from the 0.6% rise in the second quarter. This rise is also higher than the 1.3% observed in the third quarter of 2025. Accommodation services experienced notable increases, with guesthouses up 11.4% and hotels up 10.1% year-on-year.

Boa Vista island recorded the highest year-on-year price variation at 8.6%, followed by São Vicente at 7.5% and Santo Antão at 7%. Sal saw a 6.3% increase, and Santiago had a 3% rise. Restaurants saw prices increase by 1.9% and cafes, bars, and similar establishments by 0.5% compared to the third quarter of 2025.

cv.headline: Cape Verde government invests in Praia road upgrades
cv.dek: The government will rehabilitate and asphalt roads in the capital, Praia, with World Bank support.
paragraphs: The Cape Verdean government has announced a significant investment in the rehabilitation and asphalting of key roads in Praia, the capital city. The announcement was made by the Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Territorial Planning, Carlos Tavares, during a visit to the municipality. The project includes repairs between Quebra Canela and Vila Nova, as well as along Avenida dos Combatentes da Liberdade da Pátria, near Electra. Drainage work is also planned to address flooding in low-lying areas.

Minister Tavares stated that the projects are being finalized in coordination with the Praia Municipal Chamber, with works expected to commence soon. He emphasized a focus on structural improvements rather than rushed interventions to ensure lasting enhancements to traffic flow. While awaiting the larger structural works, the government will address immediate road safety issues, such as potholes.

The initiative is supported by the World Bank and involves collaboration with the Praia Municipal Chamber to ensure quality and relevance to the population's needs. Additional projects to ease traffic congestion in Vila Nova are also funded by the World Bank. Minister Tavares highlighted the importance of government and municipal coordination for urban mobility challenges in the capital.

cv.headline: Barbosa elected leader of opposition parliamentary group
cv.dek: Emanuel Barbosa will lead the Movement for Democracy's parliamentary group, aiming to foster internal cohesion and present a responsible opposition.
paragraphs: Emanuel Barbosa was elected on Monday, October 20, in Praia, as the new leader of the parliamentary group for the Movement for Democracy (MpD), the main opposition party. Celso Ribeiro, Sandra Galina, Liver Gomes, and Ivone Cardoso were appointed as vice-presidents. The new leadership aims to strengthen internal unity, leverage the experience of its deputies, and establish a responsible, dialoguing, and proactive opposition.

Barbosa stated that the group will offer qualified opposition, criticizing when necessary but also presenting concrete proposals. This leadership transition follows the national convention that elected Paulo Veiga as the MpD's national president. The elected leader emphasized the importance of dialogue, proximity, and listening to citizens, ensuring parliamentary actions reflect the concerns of Cape Verdeans.

The new leadership reaffirmed its commitment to constructive opposition, maintaining oversight of government actions and openness to dialogue in matters of national interest. The previous leader, Luís Carlos Silva, resigned following changes to party statutes that mandated a renewal of the parliamentary group's leadership within 15 days of the national convention.

cv.headline: Red Cross strengthens drought prevention in vulnerable communities
cv.dek: The Red Cross in Cape Verde is implementing a protocol to protect livelihoods and prepare communities for drought before crises occur.
paragraphs: The president of the Cape Verde Red Cross, Arlindo Carvalho, emphasized the need for proactive measures against drought to safeguard populations and minimize human and material losses. He stated that intervening before a crisis allows for alleviating suffering and preventing potential loss of life, rather than just reacting to save lives and reduce hardship after the fact.

The protocol includes measures for livelihood protection, community preparedness, and training response teams. Initially, actions will focus on Boa Vista, Porto Novo municipality in Santo Antão, and specific municipalities on Santiago island, identified by a study as areas significantly affected by drought. The International Federation is a partner in this initiative.

Carvalho explained that while the current phase targets specific areas, the possibility of extending the program to other islands remains open. The project is supported by a study that pinpoints the most visible drought-affected regions, guiding the direct intervention efforts in this first phase.

cv.headline: Cape Verde reports 1,400 viral conjunctivitis cases
cv.dek: Sal island health authorities confirm a viral conjunctivitis outbreak with 1,400 cases, primarily affecting children and hotel workers.
paragraphs: Health authorities on Sal island, Cape Verde, reported approximately 1,400 cases of viral conjunctivitis on Monday, October 20. The outbreak saw a peak of 429 cases in one epidemiological week. The Secretary of State for Health, Artur Veiga, stated the situation is under control and urged the public to remain calm, emphasizing there is no cause for alarm or extreme measures.

A national technical team will be dispatched to bolster epidemiological investigation and support the Sal Regional Health Delegation and Hospital. The clinical presentation aligns with viral conjunctivitis, predominantly impacting children, young people, and hotel industry employees. Investigations on 644 cases revealed no hospital admissions.

While the specific causative agent is awaiting confirmation from samples sent to the Pasteur Institute in Dakar, epidemiological analysis indicates the average age of those affected is 16 years. Chã de Matias is identified as the most critical area, accounting for 45 percent of analyzed cases due to its population density.

td.headline: Chad launches project to boost legume and fodder crop value chains
td.dek: The TARSPro II project aims to empower women economically and improve food security in Mayo-Kebbi Ouest province.
paragraphs: The TARSPro II project, lot 2, was officially launched on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, in Pala, Mayo-Kebbi Ouest province. The initiative, presided over by the provincial government delegate Abdelmanane Kathab, focuses on intensifying legume and fodder crop value chains. Its objectives include the economic empowerment of women, enhancing agricultural production, and strengthening nutritional security within the province.

Neyom Toukoua Djaba, the consortium coordinator and president of the Association of Women for Self-Promotion (AFAP), stated that the launch represents a significant step for the province's agricultural transformation. TARSPro II, an acronym for 'Agricultural Technologies and Innovations for Increased Resilience of Production Systems and Family Farms,' is funded by the Swiss Directorate for Development and Cooperation (DDC).

The project is being implemented by the West and Central African Council for Agricultural Research and Development (CORAF) across five countries: Chad, Niger, Benin, Burkina Faso, and Mali. This initiative seeks to build resilience in agricultural systems and support family farms through technological advancements and innovative practices.

td.headline: South Sudan condemns deadly market bombing in Abyei
td.dek: Juba demands an investigation and emergency humanitarian access after an October 19 airstrike on Amiet market caused civilian casualties and damage.
paragraphs: The South Sudanese government has strongly condemned an airstrike on Amiet market in the Abyei region on October 19, 2026. The attack resulted in significant loss of life, numerous injuries, and substantial material damage. The Office of the President issued a statement on October 21, expressing condolences to the bereaved families and solidarity with the people of Abyei, emphasizing that markets, vital for community commerce and sustenance, should not be sites of conflict.

In its official communication, Juba called for an immediate cessation of violence that endangers civilians. The government is demanding a thorough investigation to bring those responsible to justice. Furthermore, it is requesting secure access for medical personnel and humanitarian aid to reach the affected area. The authorities also urged the public to remain calm and reject retaliation.

South Sudan affirmed its commitment to protecting its citizens and announced coordinated investigations into the incident. The government aims to prevent future attacks and ensure the safety of its people. The condemnation highlights the ongoing security concerns in the Abyei region and the government's stance against such violent acts impacting civilian populations.

td.headline: African Union Commission president reaffirms human rights commitment
td.dek: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf pledged continued dedication to dignity, justice, and equality on the 40th anniversary of the African Charter.
paragraphs: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, president of the African Union Commission, reaffirmed the institution's commitment to human dignity, justice, and equality. This statement was made on the occasion of Africa Human Rights Day, which this year commemorates the 40th anniversary of the entry into force of the African Charter.

Youssouf emphasized the commission's dedication to upholding the principles of human rights and fundamental freedoms, as outlined in the Union's instruments. He highlighted the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights as a cornerstone of the African human rights framework.

The day's observance underscores the ongoing importance of these rights and freedoms across the continent. The 40th anniversary of the charter's implementation serves as a significant milestone in the pursuit of these values.

td.headline: Chad youth face bleak future due to poor health and education
td.dek: Young Chadians are seen as a burden, with public services in health and education increasingly outsourced to the private sector.
paragraphs: Chad's youth, comprising 60% of the active population, are largely overlooked in public policy, despite being lauded for their resilience. Instead of being viewed as a potential asset, this demographic is often treated as a social burden, with their future jeopardized by a lack of adequate health and education. Many young people are falling prey to drug abuse, recruitment by terrorist groups and traffickers, or dying in perilous journeys across deserts and seas.

The health of young Chadians is a significant concern, with widespread issues including infections like STIs and tuberculosis, malnutrition, and psychosomatic disorders, diabetes, and hypertension linked to stress. Education is also suffering, as the state, overwhelmed, has indirectly outsourced these critical services to the private sector. Without effective oversight, private institutions are providing substandard services, often of lower quality than what public facilities would offer.

This shift towards private provision means that schools, clinics, and hospitals are operating as commercial entities, substituting for the state's role. This trend has extended into security and even justice, indicating a broader withdrawal of public services. The consequence is a generation facing diminished opportunities due to compromised health and education, impacting their ability to thrive in a knowledge-based global landscape.

dj.headline: RPP Leaders Convene in Ali Sabieh for Strategic Political Retreat
dj.dek: The ruling party is holding a three-day meeting to discuss national, regional, and global challenges following the recent presidential election.
paragraphs: The RPP party has opened a political retreat in Ali Sabieh, focusing on future challenges and national, regional, and global issues. Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed emphasized the need to listen to the population's expectations and to "lucidly look at the challenges ahead." The meeting, themed "What party in the face of new stakes and national, regional, and global challenges?", aims to develop orientations for the party to better meet public demands.

This gathering follows the April 10 presidential election, which saw the re-election of President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh. The Prime Minister acknowledged the welcome from local authorities and the population, particularly the youth, and thanked the prefecture, regional council, security forces, and organizing teams. He stressed that a great party serves its people and nation, urging RPP officials to use the three days for reflection and preparation.

The RPP's deliberations are intended to address the evolving regional and international environment and their implications for Djibouti, a strategically positioned country at the entrance to the Red Sea. The party seeks to adapt its approach to better serve the nation's interests and the aspirations of its citizens in a changing global landscape.

dj.headline: Djibouti Adopts AI Strategy Focused on Skills and Governance
dj.dek: The nation's artificial intelligence roadmap prioritizes cybersecurity, training, research, and innovation to prepare its workforce for emerging technologies.
paragraphs: Djibouti has launched a national strategy to guide the development of artificial intelligence, emphasizing governance, cybersecurity, training, research, innovation, and inclusion. The plan follows discussions on the country's readiness for AI, with a UNESCO RAM report presented during the second day of deliberations. Experts from UNESCO and ESCWA, alongside local academics, contributed to shaping the strategy.

Key areas of focus include data governance, digital security, institutional frameworks, and national priorities. Participants highlighted that successful AI transformation hinges on developing appropriate skills, rather than solely on technology. The strategy aims to equip both public and private sectors with necessary expertise and foster a new generation of researchers and entrepreneurs in emerging technologies.

Discussions also covered essential elements for implementation, such as evolving educational programs, teacher training, research development, computing infrastructure, and university partnerships. Five panels were dedicated to elaborating on these strategic directions, underscoring a commitment to practical application and capacity building.

dj.headline: Djibouti Social Protection Model Inspires Comorian Delegation
dj.dek: Comorian officials are examining Djibouti's social welfare system, including its national social security fund and the Al Shifa hospital.
paragraphs: A delegation from the Comoros is visiting Djibouti to study its social protection and health systems, seeking opportunities for cooperation. The Comorians are particularly interested in the operational framework of Djibouti's National Social Security Fund (CNSS), which oversees social welfare and the recently opened Al Shifa hospital.

Discussions focused on the governance of social protection, coverage, healthcare facility management, and human resources. The delegation also inquired about the management and operational strategies of the Al Shifa hospital, which began operations in late June under the CNSS. Djibouti's Minister Yonis Ali Guedi highlighted recent reforms in social protection and emphasized the value of South-South cooperation.

Minister Guedi stated that sharing experiences could strengthen cooperation and lead to solutions tailored to each nation's circumstances. He assured the Comorian delegation that Djibouti's Ministry of Labor and the CNSS are open to continued dialogue and exploring potential areas for collaboration.

sz.headline: Eswatini calls for regional action on supply chain woes
sz.dek: The kingdom's foreign minister urged stronger cooperation to counter rising costs and trade disruptions affecting COMESA nations.
paragraphs: Eswatini's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Pholile Shakantu, has called for enhanced regional collaboration to address the impact of global supply chain disruptions. Speaking at the 21st COMESA Meeting of Ministers of Foreign Affairs in Harare, Zimbabwe, Shakantu highlighted how these issues are driving up the cost of living through increased fuel and shipping expenses, and delays in essential goods movement.

Shakantu emphasised that the consequences of these disruptions extend beyond trade, posing significant risks to economic stability, food security, and the general welfare of citizens across the COMESA region. The meeting also reviewed the regional peace and security situation, acknowledging its critical role in fostering economic development and shared prosperity.

The ministers recognised that collective action and sustained collaboration are necessary to tackle the region's challenges. Strengthening regional partnerships, they concluded, will better equip COMESA member states to safeguard their economies, support vulnerable populations, and promote a more stable and prosperous future for all.

sz.headline: Eswatini stars close in on Zimbabwe league title
sz.dek: Hardrock FC, featuring five Eswatini internationals, needs three wins to secure the Castle Lager Premier Soccer League championship.
paragraphs: Hardrock FC stands three wins away from clinching the Castle Lager Premier Soccer League title in Zimbabwe, with five Eswatini international players central to their campaign. The team currently holds a five-point lead over defending champions Scottland FC, who have a game in hand and are competing in the CAF Champions League. Hardrock's remaining fixtures include home games against MWOS and FC Platinum, and an away match against Simba Bhora.

Scottland FC, aiming to retain the crown, will face stiff competition in their final matches against CAPS United, Chicken Inn, Herentals, and Triangle United. Hardrock's coach, Kelvin Kaindu, has cautioned his squad against complacency despite their strong position and an eight-match unbeaten streak. He emphasized the nine points still available and the need for consistency, recalling past near-misses in title races.

sz.headline: OK Foods boss offers space to young entrepreneurs
sz.dek: Lincoln Motsa has opened his new commercial premises to three young entrepreneurs, creating 29 jobs in total.
paragraphs: OK Foods Eswatini boss Lincoln Motsa has opened his new commercial premises at Ngwane Park to three young entrepreneurs. The initiative provides a platform for a car wash and a shisanyama to operate alongside his L’s Chillers Liquor and Restaurant. This setup has created 29 jobs in total, supporting the businesses of Thabang Maphalala, who runs MAPS Village Car Wash, and Sibusiso Shabangu and Sandile Mkhulisi, operators of SISAJ Shisanyama.

Motsa, who is also the Linac Group of Companies Chairperson, stated that the project aims to uplift young people and help them establish successful businesses. The arrangement allows the entrepreneurs to operate within an established commercial setting, benefiting from shared customer traffic and mutual business activity. The establishment employs nine people at the car wash, six at the shisanyama, and 10 at the restaurant, with an additional four staff for cleaning and security.

Maphalala expressed gratitude for the opportunity, highlighting it as a significant step for MAPS Car Wash's growth and brand development. He noted that many young people face challenges due to a lack of opportunity, despite their ambition. This new location is the car wash's second in the Manzini Region, supporting its expansion goals and aspirations to create more employment and establish outlets across Eswatini.

sz.headline: Pupil accuses teacher of sexual assault at high school
sz.dek: Four teachers at Sikhunyane High School are suspended amid allegations of inappropriate relationships with students, including a sexual assault claim.
paragraphs: A 17-year-old pupil at Sikhunyane High School has accused a female teacher of sexual assault, contributing to the temporary suspension of four teachers. The suspensions, involving three male teachers and one female teacher, are a safety measure while investigations into alleged romantic relationships with pupils proceed. The school committee was initially informed by the late head teacher about two pupils reporting such relationships.

The allegations surfaced throughout the year, with one case involving a mother discovering romantic conversations between her child and a teacher on a mobile phone. A Ministry of Education and Training official met with the school committee and teachers, warning them to cease any inappropriate conduct. The committee expressed shock and anger, with parents demanding the teachers' suspension, but the ministry advised patience for ongoing investigations.

The school community, including pupils, has been traumatized by the incidents, with a senior teacher stating the need for psychological support. Despite the disruption, the temporary removal of teachers has not caused disturbances, and remaining staff are working to reassure students. The incidents occurred during a critical period as pupils are writing external examinations.

sz.headline: Eswatini theatre vice-chair speaks at Johannesburg music event
sz.dek: Sizo Hlophe will address a cultural policy summit and a main conference panel at the ACCES event, focusing on music industry growth.
paragraphs: Sizo Hlophe, Vice-Chairperson of the Eswatini Theatre Club, is set to speak at the ACCES event in Johannesburg, a major pan-African music industry gathering. Hlophe, who is also involved in rejuvenating Eswatini’s oldest theatre, will participate in two sessions. His first appearance will be at a cultural policy summit focused on promoting fair culture and exchange in the performing arts, bringing together global leaders to connect policy with practical work.

Hlophe's involvement stems from his experience as an ecosystem builder and co-founder of Antidote Music and Antidote Culture Foundation, organizations that have worked to bring local music online and develop cultural programs. He has supported initiatives like the Music Cities Convention since 2023, aiming to strengthen music ecosystems globally. His work aligns with UNESCO conventions on the status of the artist and the promotion of cultural diversity.

In addition to the policy summit, Hlophe will join an international panel at the main ACCES conference. This session, moderated by Keith Kuhudzai from Kay Media, will explore how communities and independent music businesses can build sustainable international careers, focusing on developing artists and cultural organizations from smaller markets. Hlophe believes a collaborative ecosystem is crucial for industry advancement and creative growth.

ga.headline: Gabon leasing association launches to boost business finance
ga.dek: The new professional body aims to increase leasing's role in funding productive investments and company growth.
paragraphs: The Gabonese Association of Leasing Actors (AGA CB) has officially formed in Libreville, supported by the International Finance Corporation (IFC). This initiative aims to make leasing a key tool for financing investments, developing companies, and transforming the Gabonese economy. The association's creation is seen as a significant step in structuring a sector with substantial potential but currently underutilized.

During its constituent general assembly, members reviewed statutes and internal regulations to establish a framework for the new association. Ruffin Nzoghé Ndong Simore, elected president, stated that the AGA CB's creation addresses the major challenge of giving leasing a more prominent role in financing the Gabonese economy. In 2021, leasing finance stood at 22.3 billion CFA francs, representing only 2.6% of private sector financing, despite a market potential estimated between 180 and 200 billion CFA francs annually.

Leasing allows businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), to acquire necessary equipment without significant upfront capital, thereby supporting modernization, job creation, and economic diversification. Serge Bertrand Abessolo, representing the Minister of Economy, emphasized that leasing is a vital instrument for supporting private investment, especially for SMEs. The ongoing reform process, initiated in 2021, seeks to establish an appropriate legal, fiscal, and institutional framework for the sector.

ga.headline: Gabon plans to regulate revival churches
ga.dek: The interior minister announced new rules for revival churches, drawing parallels with stricter measures in Rwanda and Angola.
paragraphs: Gabon's new interior minister, Edgard Moukoumbi, has announced plans to regulate revival churches, stating that authorities will "look into what is happening inside them." This move follows similar actions in other African nations, where governments have tightened control over religious organizations.

In Rwanda, over 8,000 places of worship were closed by August 2024 as part of a crackdown that began in 2018. The country has implemented stringent legal recognition requirements, building compliance standards, and administrative fees for religious organizations. Angola, meanwhile, requires confessions to gather 60,000 signatures, with at least 1,000 from each of the country's 18 provinces, alongside notarized documents and financial disclosures for legal recognition.

These international examples highlight the potential for strict oversight in Gabon's religious sector. While the stated aim is to protect congregants and ensure safety, the experiences of Rwanda and Angola also raise concerns about potential impacts on freedom of worship and the administrative burden placed on religious groups.

ga.headline: Gabon trains officials to fight illegal timber and wildlife trade
ga.dek: A five-day workshop aims to improve the detection, investigation, and prosecution of organized criminal networks involved in exporting protected natural resources.
paragraphs: Gabon's customs and indirect rights directorate, with support from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime, is hosting a national workshop in Libreville to combat illegal timber and wildlife trafficking. The training, which began on October 19, 2026, focuses on enhancing the capabilities of law enforcement and judicial bodies to disrupt organized criminal operations that threaten the country's natural heritage. 30 participants from various national administrations are attending the event, which is funded by the European Union through the Guard Wildlife program.

The workshop addresses critical areas such as identifying fraudulent permits, recognizing timber species, inspecting cargo, and tracing illicit financial flows. Participants will engage in practical exercises, including at the port of Owendo, to refine their skills in controlling goods and building stronger cases for prosecution. The initiative aims to improve the entire chain of repression, from detection to judicial proceedings, to better tackle the economic, ecological, and judicial challenges posed by these illegal activities.

The training emphasizes institutional cooperation between customs, forestry services, investigators, and judicial authorities. This collaborative approach is seen as crucial for effective intelligence sharing, tracking resource flows, and dismantling the financial networks supporting illegal trade. The workshop is part of ongoing efforts in Gabon to secure its significant forest and wildlife resources, which are vital national assets.

ga.headline: Eramet reinforces cervical cancer screening in Haut-Ogooué
ga.dek: The mining group donated diagnostic and treatment equipment to two hospitals as part of the "Octobre Rose" campaign.
paragraphs: The Eramet Group has donated equipment for diagnosing and treating cervical lesions to the Amissa University Hospital Center in Franceville and the Marcel Abéké Hospital (HMA) in Moanda. The handover, which took place on October 19, is part of the "Octobre Rose" campaign aimed at strengthening local health facilities' capacity for prevention, early detection, and management of human papillomavirus (HPV), a primary risk factor for cervical cancer.

This initiative follows a pilot study conducted from March to June 2025 in Haut-Ogooué, under the patronage of the Ministry of Health, which screened over 200 women aged 35 to 65. The study revealed a 19% overall HPV prevalence, indicating that nearly one in five women tested positive, though not all had cancerous lesions. Awareness campaigns in Moanda, Mounana, Bakoumba, and Sucaf also engaged hundreds to encourage screening.

Eramet acquired a digital colposcope and a thermocoagulator in 2026 to enhance diagnosis and treatment. These donations to Franceville and Moanda follow an earlier provision to Libreville's CHU in summer 2026. The company also plans to fund rapid test kits and midwife training, aligning with its "Act for Positive Mining" CSR roadmap to ensure lasting local capacity building.

ga.headline: Gabon revokes mining permits after audit
ga.dek: The Ministry of Mines has cancelled research and exploitation permits for several companies for failing to meet legal requirements.
paragraphs: Gabon's Ministry of Mines and Geological Resources has revoked mining permits from multiple operators following an audit conducted between June 29 and October 16, 2026. The decision, announced on October 19, 2026, returns these permits to state control due to non-compliance with legal and regulatory standards. This action follows a June 22, 2026, suspension of small-scale gold mining activities nationwide.

The audit specifically examined adherence to Law No. 037/2018 of June 11, 2019, which governs the mining sector in Gabon. The ministry stated that controls revealed breaches of legal and regulatory requirements by several permit holders. Consequently, permits for research and exploitation across various provinces, including Ogooué-Ivindo, Woleu-Ntem, and Ngounié, have been cancelled. Affected companies include Abice Mining Gabon, Afrique Resources SA, and SMO, among others.

The Ministry of Mines urges interested parties to contact its services for further information regarding the implementation of this decision. The authorities aim to enforce the regulatory framework for mining activities and strengthen oversight of issued titles. The ministry also warned that non-compliant entities could face legal prosecution.

gm.headline: Gambia receives $2.5M forfeited Jammeh U.S. fund
gm.dek: The Reparations Commission confirmed receipt of the money from the sale of former President Yahya Jammeh’s Potomac property.
paragraphs: The Gambia Reparations Commission has received USD 2,573,414.10 from the forfeiture and sale of former President Yahya Jammeh’s property in the United States. The funds were deposited directly into the Reparations Fund account at the Central Bank of The Gambia. The commission stated these funds will be used exclusively for the payment of reparations to eligible victims.

This development is considered a significant step in implementing the commission's mandate under the Victims Reparations Act, 2023. The funds are intended to support swift and comprehensive reparations, which can include individual or collective restitution, compensation, and rehabilitation for victims and survivors.

The commission acknowledged the cooperation between the Gambian and United States governments in facilitating the transfer of these proceeds. It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and responsible management of the funds, ensuring they are used solely for reparations and meet the needs of victims and survivors.

gm.headline: Gambia moves to ratify WIPO treaty protecting musicians
gm.dek: The National Assembly is considering a World Intellectual Property Organization treaty to safeguard artists' digital rights and earnings from piracy.
paragraphs: The Gambia is moving to strengthen protections for musicians and record producers against online piracy by ratifying the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Performance and Phonograms Treaty. Attorney General Dawda A. Jallow presented the motion to the National Assembly, explaining that the treaty, adopted in 1996, aims to protect artists as music consumption shifts to digital platforms like streaming and social media.

Jallow told lawmakers that while Gambian musicians reach global audiences digitally, their work is vulnerable to unauthorized copying and sharing, leading to no financial return. He stated that piracy deprives the state of revenue and discourages investment in creative industries. Ratification would enable Gambian collecting societies to gather royalties from digital uses and update the Copyright Act of 2004.

Lawmakers supported the motion, with one member highlighting the increasing importance of protecting creative work due to artificial intelligence advancements. The treaty would grant performers and producers rights over recorded performances and online use, ensuring they are rewarded for their efforts and protecting their reputations from harmful alterations.

gm.headline: China Day celebrates Gambia-China ties with food and culture
gm.dek: The West Africa Food Festival featured a 'China Day' event to strengthen relations through culinary exchange and cultural performances.
paragraphs: Gambia's Tourism Minister Abdoulie Jobe described food as a bridge for strengthening relations between The Gambia and China during China Day at the 2026 West Africa Food Festival (WAFFEST). The event, held from October 15 to 21, gathered members of the Chinese community, the Chinese medical team, and chefs to celebrate Chinese cuisine and heritage. Jobe stated that culinary exchange serves as a tool for tourism, cultural understanding, and international cooperation, reinforcing longstanding ties and extending friendship to other participating nations.

China's Deputy Ambassador to The Gambia, Zhao Shangsen, praised the Chinese community for integrating with local communities and highlighted China Day as an opportunity for cultural exchange, including providing a meal for guests. The Chinese medical team also showcased traditional Chinese medicine and offered medicinal soup at a festival booth. Zhao thanked the organizers and the Tourism Ministry for their support, noting the community's contribution to strengthening cultural ties.

The celebration included cultural performances by Chinese community associations and showcased the skills of Chinese culinary professionals. China Day was part of WAFFEST 2026, which brought together participants from over 30 countries under the theme “Developing Skills, Changing Lives.” The festival aimed to celebrate culinary heritage, promote professional exchange, and explore tourism development and regional cooperation, adding an international dimension to the event.
